confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:14 — "The root has role=list, but comments assume children use role=article; that is not equivalent to listitem and not enforced."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and worse than filed. Live: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets role="list"; demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 sets role="article" on the card root. `grep -rn 'role="listitem"' demo/` returns ZERO hits repo-wide, so the list owns no required children in ANY state. ARIA 1.2 gives role=list "Required Owned Elements: listitem" — this is a direct axe-core `aria-required-children` (serious) violation on both live mounts (BrowsePane.vue:80, PalettesPane.vue:75). The corpus stopped at the populated case; the empty case is also broken — PaletteCardGrid.vue:21-31 renders EmptyState as the list's only child, whose root is role="status" (EmptyState.vue:28). So the list has zero listitems whether populated or empty. Net AT effect: item count is never announced and list navigation commands do not traverse the cards. The in-source comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 states the intent ("each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark") — a role=list is not a landmark, and article is not a listitem, so the comment encodes the error rather than a missing convention.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:14 — "contain: content is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow"; challenge-D-design.md:16 — "contain: content is a performance choice with visual consequences for overflow … those consequences are not part of the design contract."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — the right surface, with a live carrier neither axis found and neither could have, since neither read the shadow token. PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 sets `contain: content` (= layout paint style); paint containment clips ALL descendant painting to the element's padding box. The grid at PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 is `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3` with NO padding, so each PaletteCard's border-box is flush with the grid's padding edge. Every card carries `cartoon-surface` (PaletteCard.vue:19) plus a `.cartoon-cast` child (PaletteCard.vue:30). The token is LEFT-offset: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css → `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` and `--shadow-cartoon-lg: -4px 4px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …, -11px 11px 0 …`. So 7px (resting) to 11px (hover) of every card's three-ply cartoon cast sits OUTSIDE the grid's left padding edge and is clipped away. `.cartoon-cast` (glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css) compounds it: `position:absolute; inset:0; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); translate: calc(-1 * var(--cast-travel) …)` with `--cast-travel: calc(6px * var(--motion-weight) * var(--cartoon-press-t))` and `scale: var(--cast-spread)` up to 1.18 — on press the cel travels a further 6px LEFT before its own -7px shadow, ~13px+ beyond the clip edge. This fires on every card in both live panes (BrowsePane.vue:92, PalettesPane.vue:82). REFUTED LIMBS: the axes blamed "sticky descendants, and positioned affordances" — both false here. SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37 uses `<Teleport to="body">` and PaletteCardMenu.vue:2 uses reka-ui DropdownMenu, which portals; both escape containment cleanly. The sole real casualty is the cartoon cast — i.e. the card system's signature register, silently amputated by its own container.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:15 — "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one empty bit."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ON THE FILTERED-ZERO LIMB ONLY — and that limb is a live user-visible falsehood the corpus never demonstrated. `empty` is bound to a SEARCH-FILTERED length at both call sites: BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` where displayedBrowse derives from pm.filteredBrowse (useBrowsePalettes.ts:43 `useFilteredList(remotePalettes, deps.searchQuery, …)`), and PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` (usePalettePorts.ts:112-114 `useFilteredList(savedPalettes, searchQuery, (p,q) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q))`). But the copy passed is unconditionally TRUE-EMPTY copy: BrowsePane.vue:84-86 "· the commons ·" / "No published palettes here yet." / "Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall." and PalettesPane.vue:78-80 "· empty plate ·" / "No saved palettes yet." / "Add colors above, then save the set." So a user holding 20 saved palettes who types a non-matching query is told "No saved palettes yet" and instructed to create one — a false statement about their own data, plus a dead-end with no clear-search affordance in the plate. REFUTED LIMBS: "loading" and "transport failure" are NOT missing — BrowsePane.vue:40-78 owns a three-way `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` with PaletteCardSkeleton for loading and `EmptyState variant="error"` + a real Retry button for transport failure; "permission-denied" has no referent in this surface. The prescribed cure ("the grid should own a typed state") is also misaimed: state is correctly owned one level up at the pane; the actual fix is consumer-side filter-aware copy.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:13 — "The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external $el consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, with a sharper proof than filed: a guard EXISTS, names the invariant, and does not test it — which is worse than absence. The coupling is real and load-bearing: PalettesPane.vue:180-183 `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid>|null>(null); const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement|undefined); useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, {handle: '.drag-handle', …})`. e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72 reads `// PaletteCardGrid is role="list" — the B.W1 single-root invariant.` then asserts only `await expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`. A fragment root does not remove the role="list" div — it only makes $el resolve to the leading comment node — so this assertion stays GREEN while drag-to-reorder silently dies. Two further gaps: the assertion runs in the **Browse** block (walk.spec.ts:67-73), the pane that never touches $el, while the **Palettes** block (walk.spec.ts:57-66) — the only useSortable consumer — asserts no list at all; and the `as any` cast at PalettesPane.vue:181 erases the one type signal that could have caught it. The source comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 is currently the ONLY thing holding the invariant.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:13 — "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about $el and useSortable; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter."
killed.refutation: FLATLY FALSE — the corpus's worst error, and it inverts a live coupling into imaginary lore. PalettesPane.vue:133 `import { useSortable } from "@vueuse/integrations/useSortable"`; :180 `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)`; :181 `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)`; :183-197 `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, { handle: ".drag-handle", animation: 150, ghostClass: "opacity-30", onEnd(evt){…pm.reorderPalettes(ids)} })`; and :76 `<PaletteCardGrid ref="sortableGridRef" …>`. The drag handle the config names is rendered by the grid's own slot children (PaletteCard.vue `class="drag-handle …"` on GripVertical). The comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 therefore documents a REAL, shipping, load-bearing structural requirement — the exact opposite of folklore. Calling the app's live drag-to-reorder wiring "no relation … folklore" is a fabricated finding, and it is the stated basis for part of this axis's SOURCE-RED verdict.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:13 — "grid-cols-1 is the only built-in layout; every responsive decision arrives through gridClass. The component cannot guarantee card width, reading order, or breakpoint behavior."
killed.refutation: FALSE on both limbs. (a) ZERO responsive decisions arrive through gridClass. Exhaustive grep of demo/ for `grid-class|gridClass` returns exactly three hits: the prop declaration (PaletteCardGrid.vue:43), its binding (:5), and ONE consumer use — BrowsePane.vue:87-90 `:grid-class="'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')"`. That is a loading-opacity cue, not a column grammar. PalettesPane.vue:75-81 passes no gridClass at all. (b) `grid grid-cols-1` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4) does not fail to guarantee width/reading-order/breakpoints — it guarantees them maximally: a single 1fr track means every card is full-width at every viewport, and DOM order is visual order at every viewport, which is the strongest reading-order guarantee a grid can make. It is also the correct choice: both consumers are half-width side-by-side panes (the source names them "the twin placeholder … in BOTH side-by-side panes", PalettesPane.vue:28-29), where multi-column palette cards would not fit. The finding faults the component for a deliberate, constrained, correct decision.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:9 — "empty can contradict the default slot; there is no item count or state union to enforce exclusivity"; challenge-D-design.md:11 — "A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither."
killed.refutation: Not realizable in the live tree, and the prescribed cure is contrivance. At BOTH call sites `empty` is derived from the IDENTICAL expression that drives the v-for, so exclusivity holds by construction: BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` vs :93 `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`; PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` vs :83 `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`. The same collection is both the predicate and the source — neither "both" nor "neither" is reachable without editing a call site to deliberately lie. With two consumers, both correct, a `CollectionSurfaceState` union on a demo-local presentational leaf is exactly the contrivance the repo's standing precept forbids (feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md: no wrapper abstractions that don't exist yet). Filed as grounds for SOURCE-RED across two axes, it is a type-signature observation with zero live manifestation.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:12 — "Arbitrary gridClass can override columns, display, containment, or visibility and makes layout testing unbounded."
killed.refutation: The containment limb is FALSE by specificity, and the rest is unbounded only in theory. `contain: content` is declared inside `<style scoped>` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:47-53), so Vue's SFC compiler emits `.palette-card-grid[data-v-<hash>] { contain: content }` — specificity (0,2,0). Any Tailwind containment utility a caller could pass (`contain-none`, `contain-layout`, …) is a bare class at (0,1,0) and loses regardless of source order. Containment is therefore NOT overridable via gridClass. "Makes layout testing unbounded" is likewise refuted by enumeration: the prop has exactly one consumer passing exactly one non-layout string (BrowsePane.vue:87-90, `transition-opacity duration-fast` + conditional `opacity-50`), so the live layout surface is a single closed case, not an unbounded space.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 — "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty"; challenge-D-design.md:12 — "A true-empty surface can therefore render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy."
killed.refutation:
FALSE as worded — the annotation fields are precisely the ones that CANNOT go blank, because EmptyState designs the failure out. EmptyState.vue:90 `withDefaults(…, { variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true })`: Vue applies a declared default whenever the incoming prop resolves to `undefined`, so PaletteCardGrid.vue:25 `:eyebrow="emptyEyebrow"` with an unset prop still renders "· empty plate ·", never a blank. The hint is `v-if`-guarded at EmptyState.vue:61 `

`, so it renders or is absent — never blank. The dot trio (EmptyState.vue:39-48) is default-on. So a bare `` still renders ghosts + eyebrow: not "semantically empty", and the invitation hierarchy survives. Only `message` (EmptyState.vue:59, no default) can render an empty display line — and `message` is the statement, not an "annotation field". Both live callers pass all three strings (BrowsePane.vue:84-86, PalettesPane.vue:78-80), so there is no live manifestation of even that residue.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:10 — "v-if=\"$slots.emptyAction\" checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node"; challenge-L-library.md:12 — "$slots.emptyAction couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model."
killed.refutation: Mechanically true, consequentially inert, and both axes missed that the slot is DEAD. Exhaustive grep of demo/ for `emptyAction|empty-action` returns exactly two hits, both INSIDE the component itself (PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 and :29). No consumer anywhere passes the slot, so the guard has never once evaluated truthy in shipped code. It is also redundant: EmptyState's own `<slot name="action" />` (EmptyState.vue:64) is unguarded and renders nothing when empty, so removing the `v-if` entirely would change no rendered output. `$slots.x` is the canonical Vue idiom for conditional slot forwarding; faulting it and prescribing a "typed action model" for a zero-consumer slot inverts the priority — the real observation (dead API surface) is filed separately in `missed`.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:9 — "EmptyState is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path"
killed.refutation: The path-depth limb is not actionable: there is no alias to use. vite.config.ts declares exactly one demo-relevant alias — `{ find: "@src", replacement: path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "src") }` — plus the generated `@mkbabb/value.js` self-alias set, and T.W1 deliberately RETIRED every `@src/*` import from the demo tree (vite.config.ts:63-66: "the demo consumes value.js ONLY through the published @mkbabb/value.js subpaths … never src/ internals"). No demo-internal path alias exists, so relative specifiers are the only mechanism and the house idiom throughout: BrowsePane.vue:189 `"../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue"`, :196 `"../shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue"`, :180 `"../ui/card"`. PaletteCardGrid.vue:36 `"../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue"` is the same idiom at its own nesting depth. Faulting it as a library-boundary defect describes the repo's ratified import convention, not a fault in this leaf. (The second limb — no shared loading/error primitive — is adjudicated under D5, where the pane-level state machine refutes it.)

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:10 — "gridClass?: string exports raw styling authority to every consumer, defeating a stable library API and allowing incompatible column grammars."
killed.refutation: Over-severity against an enumerable live surface, and the containment half is separately refuted under C4. "Every consumer" is two, and only ONE passes the prop (BrowsePane.vue:87-90) with a two-utility opacity/transition string; PalettesPane.vue:75-81 omits it. No "column grammar", incompatible or otherwise, is passed anywhere in the tree. A `class`-style passthrough on a presentational leaf is also standard practice across this very codebase — the sibling EmptyState is invoked with `class="col-span-full"` at PaletteCardGrid.vue:23 by the same pattern. There is no "library API" being defeated: PaletteCardGrid is not exported from the package (src/), only from demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:5, i.e. it is demo-internal by construction.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:11 — "Default and named slots are unconstrained. The root's list semantics depend on undocumented child behavior."
killed.refutation: The load-bearing word "undocumented" is FALSE, and the real defect is filed elsewhere. PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 documents the child contract explicitly and by name in the template: `<!-- role="list" — each child PaletteCard (role="article") sits in a list landmark. …`. The dependency is documented at the exact point of risk; what is wrong is the CONTRACT itself (article ≠ listitem), which is confirmed under D4 with full ARIA provenance. This row misdiagnoses a documented-but-incorrect contract as an undocumented one, which points a reader at the wrong cure (write docs) instead of the right one (emit listitem semantics). The "slots are unconstrained" limb is generic to every Vue slot and carries no defect on its own.

missed.claim: The role="list" root has no accessible name — neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby — so AT users get two identically anonymous lists in the same app.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:2-6 declares `role="list"` with only class bindings; there is no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title, and the component exposes no prop to supply one (PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44 declares only empty/emptyText/emptyEyebrow/emptyHint/gridClass). Both live mounts are therefore unnamed: BrowsePane.vue:80-91 and PalettesPane.vue:75-81. The surrounding code shows the team knows the idiom and applied it to the SIBLING containers but not the grid — BrowsePane.vue:47 `aria-label="Loading palettes"` on the skeleton grid and :128 `aria-label="Loading more palettes"` on the load-more grid are both named, while the actual content list between them is not. Consequence: in a screen-reader element/list rotor the user sees two unlabeled "list" entries and must enter each to discover whether it is the commons or their own saved palettes. All three axes discussed the root's list semantics (D:14, L:11) without noticing the name is absent. Cure is one attribute, no structural change.

missed.claim: The emptyAction slot and its v-if guard are dead API surface — zero consumers in the entire demo tree — while the empty plates that would need a CTA are the ones shipping without one.
missed.proof: `grep -rn 'emptyAction|empty-action' demo/` returns exactly two hits, both inside the component that declares it: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 `<template v-if="$slots.emptyAction" #action>` and :29 `<slot name="emptyAction" />`. Neither consumer passes it (BrowsePane.vue:80-118, PalettesPane.vue:75-98 contain only the default-slot v-for). The source comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:19-20 asserts "The CTA slot survives on the caption" — it survives in the template and is invoked nowhere. This matters beyond dead code because the pane that most needs the CTA is the one omitting it: PalettesPane's true-empty hint (PalettesPane.vue:80) is "Add colors above, then save the set." — an instruction with no actionable control, while the wired affordance to supply one already exists and is unused. Both C (:10) and L (:12) critiqued the guard's MECHANISM in detail; neither checked whether the slot has a single caller. Contrast with the sibling error plate, which does use the action slot correctly (BrowsePane.vue:68-77, a real Retry Button).

unproven: min-h-[120px] (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4) combined with the grid default `align-content: normal` (which computes to `stretch` for grid containers) will distribute leftover space into the single auto-sized row when exactly one card is present, stretching that card taller than its natural height and leaving a dead band of bg-well below its meta row. The CSS mechanism is decidable statically and does hold; whether it VISIBLY fires depends on a PaletteCard's natural rendered height being under 120px, which cannot be measured without a browser under probe parsimony. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE: measure a single-card My Palettes grid at PalettesPane.vue:75. If natural height >= 120px the min-h never binds and this is a no-op.
superlatives: S-1 · The single-root invariant is documented AT the point of risk, in the one place a future editor would break it. PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 places its explanatory comment as the div's FIRST CHILD rather than a sibling, and says why in-line: "a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component, and PalettesPane reads $el for useSortable — a fragment root resolves $el to the comment node, not the <div>." The comment's own POSITION is the defensive act, and it names the exact downstream consumer. Provenance: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 <-> PalettesPane.vue:180-183. This is the precise coupling challenge-L-library.md:13 dismissed as "folklore".

S-2 · Exclusivity is achieved by derivation instead of enforcement — the cheapest correct design. At both call sites the `empty` predicate and the v-for source are the SAME expression (BrowsePane.vue:83 vs :93 on displayedBrowse; PalettesPane.vue:77 vs :83 on pm.filteredSaved.value), so the contradictory state two axes demand machinery against (C:9, D:11) is unreachable without a deliberate lie at a call site. A 53-line leaf gets the guarantee for free that a CollectionSurfaceState union would have charged an abstraction for.

S-3 · State is owned at the correct altitude, and the precept is written down. BrowsePane.vue:40-78 runs loading / transport-error / populated as one `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` — PaletteCardSkeleton plates for loading (:49-53), `EmptyState variant="error"` with a real Retry Button and the machine string on a detail line for failure (:61-78), the grid for populated (:80). EmptyState.vue:2-13 states the governing rule verbatim: "TWO species, never conflated (SYNTHESIS §2.4 — loading != empty, error != empty)". The grid stays a presentational leaf on purpose; challenge-D-design.md:20's demand that it "own a typed state" would pull state DOWN from where it correctly lives.

S-4 · EmptyState designs out the exact blank-field failure challenge-D-design.md:12 predicts. `eyebrow` carries a default (EmptyState.vue:90 `{ variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true }`) so it cannot render blank even when the caller passes undefined; `hint` is `v-if`-guarded (EmptyState.vue:61) so it renders or is absent, never empty; `dots` defaults on. Every annotation field is structurally incapable of the blank state the audit predicted — and EmptyState.vue:94-105 additionally threads the certified `--ink-muted` contrast rung rather than a static muted token, with the 3.84:1 light-mode failure it replaced recorded in the comment.

confirmed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel; `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaginationBar/challenge-L-library.md:9. LIVE: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8 and :22 pass `variant="outline"`; PaginationBar.vue:34 imports from demo/ui/button/index.ts:1 = `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (a one-line forwarding barrel — 22 demo files use it, 0 import Button directly). Installed producer is @mkbabb/glass-ui 7.0.0; node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 declares ButtonProps = {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class} — NO `variant`. Compiled bytes confirm the runtime props list (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js, `props:{emphasis,tone,size,iconOnly,loading,type,disabled,class,asChild,as}`) and there is no `inheritAttrs:false`, so `variant` falls through onto the rendered <button> as a literal non-standard DOM attribute. Not a functional break — the buttons render at the producer default `emphasis:"secondary"` — hence MINOR, not the file's blanket SOURCE-RED.

confirmed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error and invalid totals.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:11. LIVE: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:3 `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is the sole render guard, and both consumers mount the bar unconditionally as a sibling of their loading/error/empty chain (AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133), so the bar is absent during first load and during error identically to a true single page. PARTIAL REFUTATION of the clause 'invalid negative/zero totals': pageCount is clamped at the source — useAdminAudit.ts:44 / useAdminFlagged.ts:55 `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` — so a zero or negative total yields exactly 1 and hides the bar correctly. Confirmed MAJOR only because the same v-if is what makes the deletion trap unrecoverable (see missed defect #1), not for the stated conflation alone.

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation (D-2: page changes have no busy register).
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:12 and challenge-D-design.md:12. LIVE: PaginationBar.vue:10 and :24 bind `:disabled` only to `!hasPrev` / `!hasNext`; nothing is bound to a busy state. The mutators do not check the busy flag they own: useAdminAudit.ts:73-78 and useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110 call `page.value++; loadX()` with only the `hasNext` guard, while `loading` (useAdminAudit.ts:39,51,69) is written but never read as a gate. On page 1 of 3 a second Next click one tick later still satisfies `hasNext` (2 < 3), so two loads are in flight at offsets 20 and 40 and both `finally` blocks clear the same boolean. The producer already ships the exact remedy and it is unused: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:16 `loading?: boolean` — 'Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles' (compiled guard at dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js: `loading || disabled` → disabled attr + click `preventDefault/stopImmediatePropagation`).

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations that are not bound to completion of the corresponding list request (D-4: rapid updates announce intermediate states).
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:13 and challenge-D-design.md:14. LIVE: PaginationBar.vue:17-19 is `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` over `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}`. `page` is incremented synchronously before the await — useAdminAudit.ts:75-76 (`page.value++; loadAuditLog()`), useAdminFlagged.ts:107-108 — so the sentence re-renders and announces on the click tick, while `entries`/`items` are only assigned after the network settles (useAdminAudit.ts:60-62, useAdminFlagged.ts:69-70). There is no commit signal between them. Correctly MINOR (announcement ordering), not SOURCE-RED.

confirmed.claim: Icon-only buttons are named, but the intended `variant="outline"` is not the current producer vocabulary; the visual hierarchy may not match the source.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:15. LIVE: the naming half is correct and good — PaginationBar.vue:11 and :25 carry `aria-label`, :14 and :28 carry `aria-hidden="true"` on the icons. The hierarchy half is confirmed: with `variant` inert the buttons resolve to the producer default `emphasis: "secondary"` (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js `emphasis:{default:"secondary"}`), which renders the `glass-wash glass-capsule` plate — a filled capsule, not the outline plate the author intended.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer or negative values are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:9. LIVE, SPLIT VERDICT. The `page>pageCount` clause is CONFIRMED and reachable: PaginationBar.vue:18 interpolates both scalars with no validation, and useAdminFlagged.ts:99 decrements `total` on delete without re-clamping `page` — with total=41 (pageCount 3) on page 3, deleting the last row gives total=40 → pageCount=2 → the bar literally renders 'Page 3 of 2' (Next disabled, Prev enabled). The `page=0` / negative / non-integer clauses are REFUTED: `page` is seeded 1 (useAdminAudit.ts:37, useAdminFlagged.ts:50), mutated only by guarded ++/-- (useAdminAudit.ts:73-85), and reset to 1 only by AdminAuditPanel.vue:114 — no live path produces them, and a NaN total makes pageCount NaN so the v-if simply hides the bar rather than printing a false label.

confirmed.claim: Events `prev`/`next` carry no target page, query generation, or request identity.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:11. LIVE: PaginationBar.vue:44-47 `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` — both payloads are empty tuples, and both consumers bind bare handlers (AdminAuditPanel.vue:88-89, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:131-132). The FACT is exact. INFO not MAJOR because the asserted consequence is separately refuted (see killed C-3): the handler re-reads the same source of truth under its own guard, so the command is well-defined without a payload. The real generation gap is in the composable, not the emit (see missed defect #3).

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances, and no threshold or large-count design exists.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:13. LIVE: PaginationBar.vue:1-31 contains exactly two commands and one label — no first/last, no page input, no ellipsis window. With `pageSize = 20` hard-coded (useAdminAudit.ts:38, useAdminFlagged.ts:51) an audit ledger of 2000 entries is 100 single-step pages. The axis correctly self-hedges ('may be correct for small sets'), so this is a design-decision gap, not a defect — INFO. Note the producer already owns windowing math the cure could reuse: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/pager-dots/pagerWindow.d.ts + PagerDots.vue.d.ts (`windowFit`, `v-model:active`, `select(index)`).

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing 'Page 1 of 2' with Previous enabled or Next disabled.
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:10. REFUTED against the live tree: PaginationBar has exactly two consumers and BOTH derive the flags as computeds from the same two scalars the label prints. useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 and useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 are byte-identical: `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))`, `hasNext = page < pageCount`, `hasPrev = page > 1`. At page 1, `hasPrev` is false by construction, so the named symptom ('Page 1 of 2' with Previous enabled) is unreachable. Call sites: AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130 — no third consumer exists (grep over demo/ returns only these two). The prop contract is unenforced, but no defect follows in shipping code.

killed.claim: `page`, `pageCount`, `hasNext`, `hasPrev` can contradict each other; the boundary should accept one normalized pagination state.
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:10 (and the file's SOURCE-RED premise at :5, 'carries pagination truth as four unrelated scalars'). REFUTED on the same evidence as C-2 — useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 / useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 make three of the four scalars pure functions of `total`+`page`, and both mutator pairs re-guard on the derived flag (useAdminAudit.ts:74,81; useAdminFlagged.ts:106,113). The four values are not 'unrelated'; they are one derived state flattened at the boundary. The prescribed cure (`PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error`) is a legitimate refactor but is prescribed for a contradiction the tree cannot express.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props.
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:11. MECHANISM REFUTED: `$emit('next')` (PaginationBar.vue:26) is dispatched synchronously inside the click handler and Vue invokes the parent listener synchronously in the same task, so no prop mutation can interleave between the child's read and the parent's handler. The handler then re-reads live state and re-guards (useAdminAudit.ts:74 `if (hasNext.value)`), making the command 'advance from whatever page is current' — idempotent with respect to any concurrent prop change. There is a real staleness bug in this area, but it is an unguarded response assignment in the composable (useAdminAudit.ts:60-62), not a parent/child prop race; see missed defect #3.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:12. REFUTED — there is no referent. `grep -rn aria-live --include=*.vue demo/` returns exactly 4 hits repo-wide: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:84 (`aria-live="off"`), demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:6,20 (a comment plus one `assertive` alert), and PaginationBar.vue:17. PaginationBar is the ONLY polite content-update live region in the application, and no second paginated surface exists (only these two admin panels page anything; AdminUsersPanel.vue and AdminNamesPanel.vue have no pagination at all). The divergence risk is hypothetical, with zero live instances.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs in glass-ui or a shared application collection package, 'not independently in each admin panel'.
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:13. The factual premise is FALSE: the pattern is NOT authored independently per panel — it is one 48-line file (demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue) imported by both of its consumers (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144), which is precisely the de-duplicated shape the finding asks for. It is also correctly scoped: demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts exports only the five panels ('hardened public surface … NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)'), keeping the bar cluster-internal. Nor does the producer duplicate it: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships pager-dots/PagerDots (a dots rail for carousels/decks, `v-model:active`) and CarouselPager/DeckPager, but no numeric prev/next data pager. Promotion to glass-ui remains a defensible design proposal; the stated defect is not real.

missed.claim: UNRECOVERABLE DEAD-END: deleting or dismissing the last item on the last flagged page hides the pagination bar with `page` still pointing past the end, and no UI path — including Refresh and a full panel remount — can get back to the remaining rows.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:98-99 (`deletePalette`) and :86-87 (`dismiss`) filter the row out of `items` and decrement `total`, but never re-clamp `page` and never re-fetch. With total=21 and pageSize=20 (:51) the admin sits on page 2 holding one row; deleting it gives total=20 → pageCount = Math.max(1,ceil(20/20)) = 1 (:55) → PaginationBar.vue:3 `v-if="pageCount > 1"` unmounts the ONLY navigation control, while `page` stays 2. AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37-41 then renders EmptyState 'No flagged palettes.' directly beneath its own toolbar reading '20 flagged' (:5-7). The Refresh button (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10) calls `loadFlagged`, which recomputes offset from the stale page — useAdminFlagged.ts:67 `(page.value - 1) * pageSize` = 20 → the API returns an empty page → the trap re-arms. Remounting the panel does not help either: the port is built once at the app root (demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:73 `const flagged = useAdminFlagged()`, provided at :245, called from demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:60 ← demo/color-picker/App.vue:351), so `page` outlives every panel unmount. Only a full page reload clears it. All three axes list this cell as something to TEST — challenge-C:15 'deletion reducing pageCount', challenge-D:19 'stale page after deletion' — but none traced it into useAdminFlagged.ts, none identified that the v-if removes the escape hatch, and none noticed that Refresh cannot recover.

missed.claim: Both consumers render the previous page's rows UNDERNEATH the loading skeletons — the `v-for` list is outside the v-if/v-else-if state chain — so while the bar already reads 'Page 2 of 3' the panel simultaneously shows 3 skeletons and 20 stale page-1 rows.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 opens the state chain (`v-if="audit.loading.value"` → skeletons), :43 `v-else-if` error, :56 `v-else-if` empty — and then :59-63 starts a NEW element `<div v-for="entry in audit.entries.value">` with no `v-else`, so it renders whenever `entries` is non-empty, including mid-load. Identical structure in AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16 / :23 / :38 / :44-48. `entries`/`items` are only overwritten after the await (useAdminAudit.ts:61, useAdminFlagged.ts:69), so every page change paints skeletons over stale rows. missed.claim: Out-of-order responses silently overwrite newer data: the pagination loaders assign `res.data` unconditionally with no request generation, sequence token, or AbortController, and the first response to settle clears the shared `loading` flag while another request is still in flight.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:60-70 — `const res = await getAuditLog(token, merged); entries.value = res.data; total.value = res.total;` with `finally { loading.value = false }`; same shape at useAdminFlagged.ts:64-78. Two concurrent loads are reachable from a double Next click (see confirmed C-4) and from the filter debounce racing pagination (AdminAuditPanel.vue:111-117 fires `page=1; loadAuditLog()` on a 300ms timer independent of any in-flight page load). If the offset-20 response lands after the offset-40 response, `entries` holds page-2 rows while the live label reads 'Page 3 of 3', and `total` is rewritten from the older snapshot. The transport offers no ordering help — demo/platform/transport/client.ts:148-155 `adminRequest` is a bare fetch that throws ApiProblem on !ok. challenge-C:15 lists 'out-of-order responses' as a required test but sites the race in the emit contract (:11), which is refuted; no axis located the actual unguarded assignment.

missed.claim: The polite live region is conditionally mounted with its content, so it cannot announce on first appearance or on disappearance — the classic broken-live-region pattern.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:3 wraps the entire bar, including the `aria-live="polite"` span at :17, in `v-if="pageCount > 1"`. The region therefore does not exist in the DOM before its first content, which is the state ARIA live regions are specified to require (a region must be present and empty/stable before mutation for reliable announcement); and the transitions that matter most — a queue crossing 2→1 pages after a deletion (useAdminFlagged.ts:99), or 1→2 pages after a refresh — remove or insert the region wholesale rather than mutating it, producing no announcement at all. challenge-C:13 and challenge-D:14 both discuss announcement TIMING; neither noticed the region's EXISTENCE is conditional. Structurally provable from source; exact AT behavior varies by screen reader.

missed.claim: The page readout uses `text-caption`, which the producer defines as ITALIC proportional type — the exact register both consumers explicitly forbid for machine strings.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:17 `class="text-caption text-muted-foreground tabular-nums px-2"`. The producer utility is italic: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css `@utility text-caption { font-family: var(--font-text); font-size: var(--type-caption); line-height: var(--type-leading-caption); font-style: italic; font-weight: 400; }` — and the demo does not override it (no `text-caption` rule anywhere under demo/styles/). Every other readout in the same two panels uses the mono, non-italic register from dist/styles/typography/utilities.css (`@utility text-mono-small { font-family: var(--font-mono); … }`): AdminAuditPanel.vue:26 ('20 entries'), :70 (timestamp, `text-small tabular-nums`), :76 (target); AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:5 ('20 flagged'), :118 (date). The panels even carry the rule in-source at AdminAuditPanel.vue:74-75 — 'a machine string is a READOUT: Fira, never italic display type (W5-12 / F-9)'. 'Page 2 of 3' with `tabular-nums` is a numeric readout rendered in italic body type. challenge-D examined visual hierarchy (:15) and missed it.

missed.claim: The two icon-only buttons never set the producer's `iconOnly` prop, forfeiting square geometry and the `data-control-target` hit-target hook that glass-ui uses to size touch targets.

"" : void 0`. With `iconOnly` unset both hooks are absent, so the chevrons render with text-button padding and no control-target sizing. challenge-L:9 named the dead `variant` but prescribed only 'emphasis/tone axes' (:15); the one producer axis that actually fixes the geometry of these two buttons is named by no axis. (Exact rendered tap-target size is not statically decidable.)

missed.claim: The hard CI typecheck gate is structurally blind to this entire defect family: `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates` is unset, so vue-tsc never reports unknown component props — the dead `variant` passes a green gate.
missed.proof: No tsconfig in the repo declares `vueCompilerOptions` (tsconfig.json, tsconfig.base.json, tsconfig.demo.json, tsconfig.lib.json all lack it; the only occurrences repo-wide are probe files under docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/SearchFilterBar/). vue-tsc 6.0.3 defaults unknown-prop checking OFF. .github/workflows/ci.yml:35 runs `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` as a hard step; I ran the identical command against the current tree and it exits 0 with `variant="outline"` live at PaginationBar.vue:8,22. So the gate that the repo treats as its type contract cannot see any dead producer prop. Every one of the three PaginationBar files reports the dead prop as a source observation without noting that the project's own gate certifies it green.

missed.claim: AdminAuditPanel's filter debounce timer is never cleared on unmount, so a pending 300ms timer fires after the panel is gone and mutates app-lifetime pagination state.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:110-117 — `let filterTimeout: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;` and a `watch` that schedules `setTimeout(() => { audit.page.value = 1; audit.loadAuditLog(); }, 300)` with no `onUnmounted`/`onScopeDispose`/`onWatcherCleanup` teardown. Because the port is an app-root singleton (usePalettePorts.ts:72, provided at :245), the late callback resets `audit.page` and issues a request against a panel the user has already left. Missed by all three axes.

missed.claim: Zero test coverage for the component and for both pagination composables.
missed.proof: The only demo test in the repo is test/demo/palettes/api/admin-palettes.test.ts (`ls -R test/demo`); grep for `useAdminAudit|useAdminFlagged` over test/ returns nothing, and the only e2e hit for pagination-ish terms is the unrelated fixture e2e/smoke/fixtures/browse-palettes.ts. challenge-C:15 demands a test matrix; the corpus never records that the current coverage is exactly zero, which is what makes the missed defects above shippable.

superlatives: The pagination state is genuinely single-sourced, which is why the corpus's headline claim collapses: useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 and useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 derive `pageCount`, `hasNext`, `hasPrev` as computeds from `total`+`page`+`pageSize`, and every mutator re-guards on its own derived flag (useAdminAudit.ts:74,81; useAdminFlagged.ts:106,113). Two independent composables, byte-identical invariants, zero drift.

Error is never costumed as empty. `loadError` is a distinct ref (useAdminAudit.ts:40) set on catch (:66) and cleared only on success (:63), and each panel renders a distinct EmptyState `variant="error"` with a Retry command ahead of the empty case (AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33). The in-code provenance ('W5-5 (F-2), the P0 case: error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger') makes the intent auditable years later.

A textbook presentational leaf: 48 lines, props in / two events out, no local state, no lifecycle, no injection, two imports (PaginationBar.vue:34-35). It is trivially testable in isolation and correctly withheld from the cluster's hardened public surface (demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts — 'NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)') while sitting beside its only two consumers.

The a11y baseline the axes take for granted is actually right and rare: aria-label on both icon commands (PaginationBar.vue:11,25), aria-hidden="true" on both decorative icons (:14,:28), aria-atomic on the live sentence (:17), and a comment carrying the wave that required it (:6 'W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels'). Compare UserSortMenu, whose aria-hidden coverage is asymmetric per the program's own axes-quality.md:224.

The transport boundary has a real error posture rather than a swallow: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:152-153 throws a typed `ApiProblem` on !res.ok, which is what lets the composables' try/catch mean something instead of masking a 500 as an empty page.

The producer defends against a defect the consumer would otherwise ship: glass-ui's Button defaults `type` to "button" when it renders a real <button> (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js `type: h.value ? p.type ?? "button" : void 0`), so the absent `type` attribute at PaginationBar.vue:7,21 is a non-defect. Worth recording precisely because it is the kind of thing a hostile reader would otherwise file.
unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE: exact screen-reader behavior for the conditionally-mounted polite region (PaginationBar.vue:3 wrapping :17) — the structural defect is source-provable, but whether NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver announce a live region inserted together with its content varies by AT and would need a real AT session.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE: the rendered tap-target size of the two chevron buttons at size="sm" without `iconOnly` — the missing `data-control-target` hook is provable from the compiled producer bytes, but whether the result falls below a 44px target needs computed styles from a running page (no browser tooling used, per probe parsimony).

UNPROVEN-DATA-DEPENDENT: the flagged-queue trap (missed defect #1) requires total > pageSize (i.e. ≥21 flagged palettes) to be reachable. The code path is unconditional and needs no unusual input, but whether production has ever exceeded 20 flagged palettes is not statically decidable.

NOT CARRIED: no motion / transition / reduced-motion claim appears in any of the three PaginationBar challenge files, so no row of docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md applies here (the file lists `PaginationBar | C · D · L` at :274 as an in-scope subject, with no M-xx assertion attached). confirmed.claim: `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent (challenge-L-library.md:9).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. Live: `demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8` and `:22` pass `variant="outline"`. The import resolves `demo/ui/button/index.ts:1` = `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` (glass-ui 7.0.0, node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json:3). `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19` declares ButtonProps = { emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class } — there is NO `variant`. `grep -o variant node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` returns ZERO hits, and `dist/components/button/styles.css` keys only on `[data-emphasis]`, `[data-tone]`, `[data-size]`, `[data-icon-only]`, `[data-loading]`. So `variant` lands as an inert HTML attribute via Vue attribute fallthrough and the authored visual intent (a bordered/outline control) never renders; the buttons take the default emphasis instead. Scope correction the axis missed: this is systemic, not local — `grep -c 'variant="'` over demo/ = 103 sites vs `emphasis="` = 2, including two more in the same file's own parent (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10,29,90,94).

confirmed.claim: Icon-only buttons are named, but intended `variant="outline"` is not the current producer vocabulary; the visual hierarchy may not match the source (challenge-D-design.md:16).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, same proof as L-1 (PaginationBar.vue:8,22 vs Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 + button/styles.css selector set). The axis's hedge ("may not match") is resolvable statically and resolves against the source: the prop is inert. The first limb — "icon-only buttons are named" — is also verified correct: `aria-label` on the button (PaginationBar.vue:11,25) + `aria-hidden="true"` on the glyph (`:14`,`:28`). D-5 stopped one step short: `iconOnly` is a REAL producer prop (Button.vue.d.ts:14) and is not passed — see missed finding M3.

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation (challenge-C-implementation.md:11).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED in substance, but MISLOCATED by the axis — the child owns no request and structurally cannot guard. The guard is missing in the composables: `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` `nextPage()` = `if (hasNext.value) { page.value++; loadAuditLog(); }` — it never consults `loading` even though `loading` is declared (`:39`) and exported (`:92`); identical shape at `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117` (`loading` at `:52`, exported `:138`). `loadAuditLog` assigns unconditionally (`useAdminAudit.ts:61-62` `entries.value = res.data; total.value = res.total`) with no request generation. Since Vue applies the new `:disabled` (PaginationBar.vue:10,24) only on nextTick, a double-activation inside one frame on a pageCount>=3 set passes both guards synchronously (hasNext recomputes 1<N true, then 2<N true) and issues two overlapping loads; the later-resolving response wins, so the audit ledger can render page-2 rows under the label "Page 3 of N" (PaginationBar.vue:18). Decisive in-repo precedent the axis missed: the sibling `demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:98` already implements exactly this guard — `if (!hasMore.value || nextCursor.value == null || loadingMore.value) return;`. On a 2-page set the guard does hold (hasNext flips false synchronously), so the axis's unqualified framing overstates by one case.

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances; no threshold or large-count design exists (challenge-D-design.md:14).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. PaginationBar.vue:1-31 contains exactly three children: prev button, label, next button — no first/last, no page input, no jump. `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:38` fixes `pageSize = 20` against an append-only admin ledger whose `total` is unbounded (`:36`, `:62` from `res.total`), so `pageCount` (`:44`) grows without limit; reaching entry #1000 costs 49 sequential clicks each with a network round-trip (`:76`). The only narrowing tools are the two exact-ish text filters (`actionFilter`/`targetFilter`, `:41-42`, applied `:56-57`). The axis's hedge "may be correct for small sets" is right in form and wrong in application here: it is correct for AdminFlaggedPanel (a queue that is meant to be drained) and incorrect for AdminAuditPanel (a ledger that only grows).

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer, or negative values are rendered verbatim (challenge-C-implementation.md:9).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED IN PART — one limb is live-reachable, three are refuted. REACHABLE: `page > pageCount`. `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:87` and `:99` decrement `total` on dismiss/delete without reloading and without clamping `page`. With total=41, page=3 (one item on the last page), deleting it gives total=40 -> `pageCount` (`:55`) = 2 while `page` stays 3 -> PaginationBar.vue:3 `pageCount > 1` passes and `:18` renders the literal string "Page 3 of 2", with Prev enabled (`:57` 3>1) and Next disabled (`:56` 3<2 false). REFUTED: `page=0`, negative, and non-integer are unreachable in the live tree — `page` is initialised to 1 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:50`, `useAdminAudit.ts:37`), mutated only by guarded +/-1 (`:105-117`, `:73-85`) and by `audit.page.value = 1` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:114); `pageCount` is `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(...))` so it can never be 0 or negative. `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-7` re-exports only the five panels — PaginationBar is not a public surface, so no third consumer can supply arbitrary values. The axis's headline survives; its stated mechanism ("contradictory inputs") does not — the reachable path is a mutator that omits a clamp, and its worst form is far more severe than "rendered verbatim" (see missed finding M1).

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations, which are not explicitly bound to completion of the corresponding list request (challenge-C-implementation.md:13).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. `PaginationBar.vue:17-19` is `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` around `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}`. `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110` increments `page.value` SYNCHRONOUSLY and only then calls the async `loadFlagged()`; `useAdminAudit.ts:73-77` is identical. The live region therefore mutates and announces on the click tick, while `items`/`entries` are only replaced when the promise settles (`useAdminFlagged.ts:69-70`, `useAdminAudit.ts:61-62`). Corroborated at the surface: `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18` swaps the list to skeletons while `:126-133` keeps the bar mounted with the already-advanced number. A screen-reader user hears "Page 3 of 12", then silence, then the rows change with no second announcement.

confirmed.claim: The live page sentence is useful, yet rapid updates could announce intermediate states before content is ready (challenge-D-design.md:15).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — same mechanism as C-5, and the axis's hedge ("could") is resolvable: it always does, not merely under rapid updates. Sync increment at useAdminFlagged.ts:107 / useAdminAudit.ts:75 precedes the async fetch at `:108` / `:76`; the region at PaginationBar.vue:17 is bound to `page`, not to request completion. The "useful" half is also verified: `grep -rn aria-live demo/ --include=*.vue` yields only 4 sites total (ComponentSliders.vue:84 is `aria-live="off"`, ErrorBoundary.vue:20 is `assertive`), so PaginationBar.vue:17 is the demo's only navigational live region.

confirmed.claim: Page changes have no busy register; users can repeatedly activate arrows while results are loading (challenge-D-design.md:13).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. PaginationBar.vue:37-42 declares four props — page, pageCount, hasNext, hasPrev — and no loading/busy input; neither call site passes one (AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133) despite `loading` being exported by both composables (useAdminAudit.ts:92, useAdminFlagged.ts:138). The producer already ships the affordance: `Button.vue.d.ts:16` `loading?: boolean` documented as "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles", with `.button[data-loading] { cursor: progress; }` in dist/components/button/styles.css. Surface proof: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 renders skeletons for the list while `:126-133` renders the bar unchanged in the same tick, so the two halves of the panel disagree about whether a request is in flight.

confirmed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`, conflating a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals (challenge-D-design.md:12).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED IN PART. The loading/unknown limb is real: `useAdminFlagged.ts:50-55` starts at total=0 -> pageCount = Math.max(1, 0) = 1 -> PaginationBar.vue:3 `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is false, so on first paint the bar is absent and then pops in after the fetch, adding a ~60px insertion (`py-3` + 36px control at `:4`) below the list — a layout shift the axis did not name. REFUTED: the "invalid negative/zero totals" limb is unreachable — `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55, useAdminAudit.ts:44) floors pageCount at 1 for every input including a negative or NaN-adjacent total. Also mitigating, and unacknowledged by the axis: during load the panels render AdminListSkeleton instead of the list (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18, AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38), so the bar's absence is not the user's only loading signal.

confirmed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase (challenge-L-library.md:12).
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED WEAKLY, with the mechanism corrected. The demo's other paginated surface is the public wall, and it announces at NO phase, not a different one: `demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:33-37,92-108` is keyset/cursor pagination with a load-more affordance, and `grep -rn aria-live demo/ --include=*.vue` shows no live region anywhere in the browse tree (the only four are ComponentSliders.vue:84, ErrorBoundary.vue:6,20, PaginationBar.vue:17). So the announcement policy is inconsistent across paginated surfaces, but the two surfaces use different paradigms (page-swap vs append), which legitimately warrant different announcement text — the axis's implied "one shared sentence" cure over-unifies. Downgraded to INFO.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props (challenge-C-implementation.md:10).
killed.refutation: REFUTED, and the prescribed cure is backwards. PaginationBar.vue:44-47 emits `prev: []` / `next: []` — zero payload — and the child holds no state of its own (PaginationBar.vue:33-48 has no ref, no computed, no watcher). Both handlers re-read the parent's OWN authoritative refs at call time: `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117` and `useAdminAudit.ts:73-85` each evaluate `hasNext.value` / `hasPrev.value` — computeds over the live `page`/`pageCount` (`:56-57`, `:45-46`) — inside the handler body. A stale child prop therefore cannot mis-navigate, because the child contributes no data to the decision. Carrying "the destination" as the axis prescribes would encode the CHILD's possibly-stale view of `page` into the event and hand it to the parent, MANUFACTURING the race the finding claims to cure. The payload-less emit is strictly the more race-resistant shape here.

killed.claim: Events `prev`/`next` carry no target page, query generation, or request identity (challenge-L-library.md:11).
killed.refutation: REFUTED on the same grounds as C-3 for the target-page limb: the parent re-derives the target from its own state (useAdminFlagged.ts:106-108, useAdminAudit.ts:74-76), so a target on the event is redundant at best and stale-propagating at worst. The request-identity limb is a real gap but is misfiled against this component: PaginationBar issues no request and observes no response (PaginationBar.vue:1-48 is a pure render of four props), so request identity can only be introduced where the fetch lives — `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` / `useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79`. That live gap is reported as confirmed C-4, not here.

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled (challenge-C-implementation.md:10).
killed.refutation: REFUTED for the live tree. At both — and only — call sites the flags ARE derived, from the same refs that feed `page`/`pageCount`, in the same synchronous computed graph: `useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57` (`pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(total/pageSize))`, `hasNext = page < pageCount`, `hasPrev = page > 1`) and `useAdminAudit.ts:44-46`, identical. AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133 pass all four from that one graph, so Vue renders a consistent snapshot and the specific stated symptom ("Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled) is not producible. No third consumer can exist: `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-7` ("hardened public surface (T.W1 F7) — NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)") deliberately does not export PaginationBar. The claim survives only as an unexercised type-level looseness, i.e. INFO, not a defect.

killed.claim: `page`, `pageCount`, `hasNext`, `hasPrev` can contradict each other; a library boundary should accept one normalized pagination state (challenge-L-library.md:10).
killed.refutation: REFUTED — same evidence as C-2 (useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57, useAdminAudit.ts:44-46, admin/index.ts:1-7). Additionally the premise is a category error: PaginationBar is not a library boundary. It is a private, unexported child of the admin cluster with exactly two in-tree consumers. The stated target — `PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error` plus a named command result (challenge-L-library.md:16) — is also structurally unsound as a cure: the parent composables already hold precisely those fields as separate refs (`loading` useAdminFlagged.ts:52, `loadError` `:53`, `page` `:50`, `pageCount` `:55`), so an ADT adds a pack/unpack layer at both ends and yields no capability the props lack. Every defect this corpus actually proved (the unclamped `page` after delete, the missing in-flight guard, the announcement phase) lives in the composables, not in the prop shape — the prescription mislocates the repair.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel (challenge-L-library.md:13).
killed.refutation: REFUTED on fact. There is no per-panel duplication: PaginationBar.vue is ONE file, imported by exactly two of the five admin panels (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144). The other three paginate not at all — grepping `page|offset|limit|loadMore` over AdminUsersPanel.vue, AdminNamesPanel.vue and AdminTagsPanel.vue yields only AdminUsersPanel.vue:338, a comment about page SCROLL. So the extraction the axis demands has already been performed. The glass-ui half is also unavailable: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/index.d.ts` exports 28 component barrels and none is pagination or pager — there is no producer home to move it to. (`PagerDots-*.js` exists as an internal build chunk but is not exported.)

missed.claim: M1 — DELETION STRANDS THE MODERATION QUEUE AND MAKES IT REPORT ITSELF EMPTY, PERMANENTLY. Removing the last item(s) on the last page drops `pageCount` to 1 while `page` stays >1; PaginationBar then hides ITSELF, leaving the operator on a nonexistent page with an empty list, a false "No flagged palettes" empty state, and no surviving control to get back.
missed.proof: `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:81-103`: both `dismiss()` and `deletePalette()` filter `items` locally and do `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` (`:87`, `:99`) with NO reload and NO clamp of `page`. Walk it: total=25, pageSize=20 (`:51`), operator on page 2 clearing its 5 rows — the routine moderation gesture. After the fifth dismiss, total=20 -> `pageCount` (`:55`) = Math.max(1, ceil(20/20)) = 1 -> `PaginationBar.vue:3` `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is FALSE and the ENTIRE bar unmounts, taking both escape hatches and the live region with it. `items` is now [] and `loading`/`loadError` are false/null, so `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37-41` renders the EmptyState "· nothing flagged · No flagged palettes." while 20 flagged palettes remain unmoderated. It does not self-heal: the panel's only other control, Refresh (`AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10`), calls `loadFlagged()` which fetches `offset = (page.value - 1) * pageSize = 20` against a 20-row set (`useAdminFlagged.ts:64-70`) and returns empty again, re-confirming the dead state. And it survives navigation: the composable is instantiated once inside `providePalettePorts` (`demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:69` `const flagged = useAdminFlagged();`, provided at `:245`), an ancestor of the panel, so unmounting and remounting the admin panel does not reset `page`. Only a full app reload recovers. This is the exact failure mode the file's own hardening forbids — `useAdminFlagged.ts:73` "a dead backend must never read as a clear queue", AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:20-21 "error != empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear moderation queue" — reintroduced through the pagination path rather than the network path. All three axes circled this without landing it: challenge-C-implementation.md:15 lists "deletion reducing `pageCount`" only as a TEST to be written, and challenge-D-design.md:12 frames the disappearance as semantic conflation, not as an unrecoverable trap. Cure (one line, in the mutators, not in this component): clamp `page` to `pageCount` and reload after any total-reducing mutation.

missed.claim: M2 — Native `disabled` on the arrows DROPS KEYBOARD FOCUS at exactly the moment the user reaches the terminal page, and the producer ships the focus-preserving alternative that would prevent it.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:10` and `:24` bind `:disabled="!hasPrev"` / `:disabled="!hasNext"` — the native attribute. A keyboard user pressing Enter on Next repeatedly reaches the last page, at which point `hasNext` (useAdminAudit.ts:45) flips false and Vue applies `disabled` to the element that currently holds focus; the element leaves the tab order and focus falls to `<body>`, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document and the user loses their place in a long ledger. glass-ui 7.0.0 explicitly supports the focus-preserving idiom as a first-class styled state — `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css` styles `.button:disabled, .button[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity: var(--opacity-disabled); cursor: not-allowed; }` and reserves the destructive half for the native form alone: `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none; }`. Every hover/press rule in that sheet is likewise written `:not(:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"])`, i.e. the producer designed for consumers to choose `aria-disabled`. The component chose the one that destroys focus. The same defect compounds with M1: when `pageCount` drops to 1, `PaginationBar.vue:3` removes the focused button from the DOM entirely. Not named on any axis — challenge-D-design.md's required cells (`:20`) list "keyboard/touch" as a matrix cell but assert nothing about focus retention. Cure: `aria-disabled` + a no-op guard in the click handler, keeping both arrows focusable and announced.

missed.claim: M3 — The producer's `iconOnly` geometry and `--ui-glyph` sizing token are both bypassed: the buttons are not square, and on any coarse-pointer device the chevrons stay pinned at 16px inside a 54px control.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:7-15` and `:21-29` pass `size="sm"` but never `icon-only`, though `Button.vue.d.ts:14` declares `iconOnly?: boolean` — "Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command" — precisely this case, and `dist/components/button/styles.css` implements it as `.button[data-icon-only] { inline-size: var(--button-size); block-size: var(--button-size); min-block-size: var(--button-size); padding: 0; }`. Without it the buttons keep the text rung's `padding-inline: calc(0.75rem * var(--ui-scale))`, rendering ~40x36 lozenges rather than 36x36 squares. This is not a style preference: the idiom is already established in this very repo at GenerateControls.vue:166,176; PalettesPane.vue:65; PaletteSlugBar.vue:20,32; CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:136. Compounding it, `PaginationBar.vue:14` and `:28` hardcode `class="h-4 w-4"` on the glyphs, which lands in Tailwind's `utilities` layer and therefore overrides glass-ui's scale-aware rule `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph) }` (authored in `@layer components`). `dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1` sets `--ui-glyph: calc(1rem * var(--ui-scale))` and `--control-h-sm: max(calc(2.25rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))`, and `dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css` raises both under `@media (pointer: coarse) { :root { --ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5); --control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); } }`. So on every touch device the control grows to 54px while the chevron stays frozen at 16px — 30% of the control where the producer designed 44%. (Tap target is NOT a defect: 54px on coarse, 40x36 on fine, both clear WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum.) challenge-D-design.md:16 got as far as noticing the producer vocabulary was stale and stopped at `variant`.

missed.claim: M4 — The pagination control is a bare `<div>`: no `nav` landmark, no accessible group name, and no `aria-controls` binding it to the list it drives.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:2-5` is `<div class="flex items-center justify-center gap-2 py-3">`. Screen-reader users therefore meet three ungrouped orphans — "Previous page, button" (`:11`), a polite live region (`:17`), "Next page, button" (`:25`) — with nothing declaring that they form one navigation control or which region they act on. The ARIA APG pattern for pagination is a `<nav aria-label="Pagination">` landmark, which would also make the control reachable by landmark navigation instead of only by sequential Tab through the whole panel. The list it drives carries no id to point at either (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:44-48 and AdminAuditPanel.vue:59 open the row loop on unidentified divs), so `aria-controls` has no target to name. All three axes graded the a11y of the BUTTONS (challenge-D-design.md:16 "icon-only buttons are named") and none graded the a11y of the CONTAINER.

missed.claim: M5 — `justify-center` plus a variable-digit label makes both arrows drift horizontally when the page number gains a digit, so the click target moves under a user who is clicking repeatedly.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:4` centers the row (`flex items-center justify-center gap-2`) and `:17-19` is a `px-2` span whose width is the natural width of "Page N of M". `tabular-nums` (`:17`) equalises the width of each digit but not the COUNT of digits, so crossing page 9 -> 10 (or 99 -> 100, well within reach of the unbounded audit ledger — see confirmed D-3) widens the label by one digit and pushes Previous and Next apart by half that each. The user paging steadily through the ledger has the Next button slide out from under the cursor at every decade boundary. Cure is one declaration: a `min-w` on the label sized to the widest expected string, or `justify-between` on a fixed-width row. No axis touched layout stability; challenge-D-design.md:20 lists "large numerals/localization" as a required cell but reads it as a typography concern, not a target-motion one.

missed.claim: M6 — Two different control rungs appear in the same panel: the pagination arrows sit at the producer's `sm` rung (36/54px) while the toolbar's refresh button is hand-clamped to 28px.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:9,23` pass `size="sm"` and add no class override, so the arrows resolve to `--control-h-sm` = 36px (54px coarse) per `dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1`. Fifteen lines above the same bar in the same rendered column, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10` writes `<Button variant="outline" size="sm" class="h-7 px-2">` — 28px — and `AdminAuditPanel.vue:30` does the same; `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:90,96` repeat `h-7 px-2` on the Dismiss/Delete row actions. So the surface presents three control heights for one semantic rung, and the vertical rhythm of the panel breaks at the pagination boundary. Worth stating precisely because PaginationBar is the CONFORMANT party here — the repair belongs in its siblings, but the visible inconsistency is a property of the surface this component terminates. Invisible to all three axes because each read PaginationBar.vue in isolation (all three receipts read "lines 1-48, source-only").

unproven: Exact assistive-technology behaviour of the `aria-live` region when it is INSERTED by `v-if` rather than mutated in place (PaginationBar.vue:3 wrapping :17) — i.e. whether the 1 -> 2 pageCount transition announces at all, announces the whole sentence, or is silently dropped. Live-decidable only, per NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver; the ORDERING defect (confirmed C-5/D-4) is proven statically and does not depend on this.

Whether the built cascade actually places Tailwind's `utilities` layer after glass-ui's `@layer components` in the SERVED bundle, which is what makes `h-4 w-4` (PaginationBar.vue:14,28) beat `--ui-glyph`. Reasoned from `demo/styles/foundation.css:1` (`@import "tailwindcss"`, which declares the layer order) plus `:56-57` (the two glass-ui imports), but not measured on a served page. Missed finding M3 stands regardless — the absent `icon-only` is a defect independently of the glyph question.

Precise rendered appearance of the fallthrough `variant="outline"` buttons — which default `emphasis`/`tone` pair the producer resolves to and whether the result reads as a bordered control by accident. The DEAD-PROP fact (confirmed L-1/D-5) is proven from the type declaration, the built bundle, and the stylesheet selector set; only the resulting pixels are unverified.

Real-world reach of the confirmed C-4 double-activation window — whether a human double-click lands both events inside one Vue tick before `:disabled` (PaginationBar.vue:10,24) is applied on nextTick. The missing guard (useAdminAudit.ts:73-78 / useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117 never consult `loading`) and the missing response ordering (useAdminAudit.ts:61-62 assigns unconditionally) are proven statically; the frame-level timing is not.
superlatives: The `tabular-nums` on the page label (PaginationBar.vue:17) is a deliberate, uncommon, correct choice: it holds the sentence's glyph advance constant so the number does not shimmer as the operator pages. Nothing required it; someone thought about what a changing numeral does to a stationary eye. (Its one blind spot — digit COUNT, not digit width — is missed finding M5, which is a refinement of a good instinct rather than an absence of one.)

The icon-button accessibility trio is exactly right and carries its own provenance: `aria-label` on the interactive element (PaginationBar.vue:11,25), `aria-hidden="true"` on the decorative glyph (`:14`,`:28`), and a comment naming the wave that fixed it (`:6` "W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels"). Verified against the whole demo, this is the majority idiom, not a local accident — the same pattern recurs at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:9-11,97-100 and PaletteSlugBar.vue:16.

It is the demo's ONLY navigational live region. `grep -rn aria-live demo/ --include=*.vue` returns four sites in the entire application: ComponentSliders.vue:84 (`off`), ErrorBoundary.vue:6 and :20 (`assertive`), and PaginationBar.vue:17. The sibling paginated surface — the public wall's keyset load-more at useBrowsePalettes.ts:92-108 — announces nothing at all. Whoever wrote line 17 chose `polite` + `aria-atomic="true"` correctly, which is the right pair for a short atomic sentence; only the PHASE is wrong (confirmed C-5).

Cluster-privacy discipline is genuinely observed. `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-7` declares "hardened public surface (T.W1 F7) — NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)" and lists the five panels; PaginationBar is deliberately absent. The result is one shared child, two consumers, zero duplication, zero leaked surface — which is simultaneously the fact that kills challenge-L-library.md:13 and the reason challenge-L's whole library-boundary frame does not apply.

Within its own panel it is the only Button call site that respects the producer's size rung untouched — `size="sm"` with no class override (PaginationBar.vue:9,23) — while AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10,90,96 and AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 all hand-clamp to `h-7 px-2`. On the one axis where the surface is inconsistent, this file is the conformant party (see missed finding M6).

48 lines, zero refs, zero computeds, zero watchers, zero lifecycle hooks: the render is a pure function of four props and the emits carry no payload (PaginationBar.vue:33-48). The presentational split is genuinely clean, and it is what makes the C-3/L-3 race allegations refutable in a single reading — a component that owns no state cannot race. Several of this corpus's prescriptions (a PaginationState ADT, request identity on the events) would have destroyed that property to fix defects that live one layer up.

Motion hygiene is clean by construction and independently corroborated: the component authors no animation, transition, or timing of its own, and the producer guards what it does supply — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .button { transition: none } }` closes dist/components/button/styles.css, under the demo's global neutraliser at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193. The motion quarantine reached the same verdict independently, listing `PaginationBar | C · D · L` under §7.4 "No motion content — vacuously cleared on this axis" (audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274). No M-row is available to carry against this component, and none is owed.
