confirmed.claim: "The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression." (challenge-C-implementation.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED — the guard exists in NAME and is VACUOUS. Live consumer: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-183 does `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid>|null>(null)` → `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement|undefined)` → `useSortable(sortableEl, …)`. The only artifact that names the invariant is e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72: `// PaletteCardGrid is role="list" — the B.W1 single-root invariant.` followed by `await expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`. That assertion passes IDENTICALLY whether the root is a single `<div>` or a dev-root Fragment (a leading root comment leaves the div — and therefore `role=list` — fully rendered; only `$el` changes, from the div to the fragment's text anchor). So the named guard cannot fail on the property it claims to guard. Worse, it runs in the **Browse** branch (walk.spec.ts:67-73); the **Palettes** branch (walk.spec.ts:57-66), the only pane that actually reads `$el`, asserts no list at all. Nor does the type system guard it: PalettesPane.vue:181 launders the reach through `as any`, so a root-shape change is invisible to vue-tsc too. Zero enforcement, type or test.

confirmed.claim: "The root has `role=list`, but comments assume children use `role=article`; that is not equivalent to `listitem` and not enforced." (challenge-D-design.md:14)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, live in both panes. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets `role="list"`; the only child element type placed in its default slot is PaletteCard, whose root is demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 `role="article"` (call sites: PalettesPane.vue:82-97, BrowsePane.vue:92-117 — both render `PaletteCard` directly into the slot with no wrapper). ARIA's `list` role has required owned elements `listitem`; `article` is not one. Consequence is deterministic, not stylistic: AT enumerates the container as a list with **0 items** while N articles sit inside it un-owned, so "3 of 12" positional announcement is lost on every saved/browsed palette. The grid's own comment (PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8) documents the WRONG expectation as if it were correct.

confirmed.claim: "`contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow or layout participation." (challenge-C-implementation.md:14) / "`contain: content` is a performance choice with visual consequences for overflow … not part of the design contract." (challenge-D-design.md:16)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED with the concrete manifestation neither axis named. PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 sets `.palette-card-grid { contain: content; }` = `layout paint style`; paint containment clips descendant painting to the box. PaletteCard.vue:19 rides `cartoon-surface`, defined at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1 as `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }`, and `--shadow-cartoon-md` resolves at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1 to `-3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` — a triple cast offset LEFT and DOWN. The grid is `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3` with NO padding (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4) and default `justify-items: stretch`, so each card's border box is flush with the grid's padding box on both horizontal edges. Therefore the entire left-hand cast (up to -7px) of EVERY card, and the bottom cast of the LAST card, fall outside the containment box and are clipped. `gap-3` (12px) > 7px, so only inter-card bottom casts survive. This silently truncates the register foundation.css:495-518 spends 24 lines of comment ratifying. No consumer can opt out — the rule is in the SFC's scoped, UNLAYERED `<style>`, which outranks any `@layer utilities` Tailwind class a caller could pass through `gridClass`. (Pixel-level confirmation would need a live render; the CSS cascade and geometry are decidable statically and are what is asserted here.)

confirmed.claim: "`empty` can contradict the default slot; there is no item count or state union to enforce exclusivity." (challenge-C-implementation.md:9) / "A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither." (challenge-D-design.md:11)
confirmed.proof: The API shape is as described — PaletteCardGrid.vue:39 `empty?: boolean` is an external prop, PaletteCardGrid.vue:12 `<slot />` is unconstrained, PaletteCardGrid.vue:22 `v-if="empty"` — but the claimed contradiction is UNREACHABLE in the live tree and the prescribed cure is unsound. Both call sites derive `empty` from the SAME expression that drives the `v-for`: PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` vs :83 `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`; BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` vs :93 `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`. The cure ("contradictory-state rejection", challenge-C:16) requires the leaf to count slot children; `$slots.default()` on a `v-for` returns a single Fragment vnode whose `children` also carries whitespace/comment nodes, so vnode-counting is a known-fragile Vue anti-pattern that would introduce a defect to police a state no caller can reach. Downgraded from the file's SOURCE-RED verdict to INFO.

confirmed.claim: "Arbitrary `gridClass` can override columns, display, containment, or visibility and makes layout testing unbounded." (challenge-C-implementation.md:12) / "`gridClass?: string` exports raw styling authority to every consumer." (challenge-L-library.md:10)

But **containment is NOT overridable**: `contain: content` lives in the SFC's scoped `<style>` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:47-53), which Vite emits UNLAYERED, and unlayered declarations beat every `@layer utilities` rule in the cascade regardless of specificity. The "unbounded layout testing" risk is also unexercised: exactly ONE of two consumers passes the prop, and passes no layout token at all — BrowsePane.vue:87-90 sends `'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')`. PalettesPane passes nothing. INFO, not SOURCE-RED.

killed.claim: "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter." (challenge-L-library.md:13)
killed.refutation: FALSE on its central assertion. The relation is live, load-bearing, and does exactly what PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 says it does: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:133 `import { useSortable } from "@vueuse/integrations/useSortable"`; :180 `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)`; :181 `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)`; :183 `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, { handle: ".drag-handle", … })`; and the handle exists at PaletteCard.vue:47-50 (`class="drag-handle …"`, gated on the `draggable` prop PalettesPane.vue:90 passes). The structural requirement is not folklore — it is a currently-SATISFIED constraint with a named consumer 3 lines long. The only defensible residue is far narrower than the claim: the reach is untyped (`as any`, :181), which is reported separately. Reporting the seam as nonexistent while the seam is the component's single reason for its root shape is the corpus's largest inversion here — and it is precisely the seam under which the two real reorder defects (see `missed`) were sitting.

killed.claim: "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty." (challenge-C-implementation.md:11) / "A true-empty surface can therefore render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy." (challenge-D-design.md:12)
killed.refutation:
FALSE as stated — "blank annotation fields" (plural) cannot occur, and the one field that could is covered by tests at both call sites. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:72-91 wraps the props in `withDefaults(…, { variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true })`, so `eyebrow` NEVER renders blank (EmptyState.vue:55-57 prints the default). `hint` is `v-if`-guarded (EmptyState.vue:61) and `detail` likewise (:23) — an absent value renders NO element, not a blank one. Only `message` (EmptyState.vue:58-60, `{{ message }}`) could yield an empty `

`. And both live consumers pass all three strings — PalettesPane.vue:78-80 and BrowsePane.vue:84-86 — with e2e oracles asserting the exact copy verbatim at e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:194-197 (`· empty plate ·` / `No saved palettes yet.`) and :230-233 (`· the commons ·` / `No published palettes here yet.`). The prescription "stable default copy" (challenge-C:16) is already satisfied one altitude up, under test.

killed.claim: "`v-if="$slots.emptyAction"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node." (challenge-C-implementation.md:10) / "`$slots.emptyAction` couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model." (challenge-L-library.md:12)

Consequence: the guard at PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 only decides whether to pass an `#action` template into EmptyState, and EmptyState renders that slot BARE — `<slot name="action" />` (EmptyState.vue:64, and :26 for the error species) with no wrapper element, no padding, no min-height. A slot function that yields nothing therefore produces nothing: no empty box, no phantom gap, no layout artifact. The failure mode the finding implies does not exist. Deadness: `grep -rn emptyAction demo/` returns exactly two hits, both inside PaletteCardGrid.vue itself (:28, :29). Neither of the two consumers passes the slot (PalettesPane.vue:75-81, BrowsePane.vue:80-91 — full prop lists, no `#emptyAction` template). The critique targets a guard on a slot nobody fills; the real finding is that it is dead code (reported under `missed`).

killed.claim: "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit." (challenge-D-design.md:15) — plus the §Required state matrix prescription that "the grid should own a typed state".
killed.refutation: The premise that the app cannot distinguish these states is FALSE; every state D demands is already owned, at the correct altitude, by composition. In BrowsePane.vue the three surfaces are SIBLING branches of one keyed `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (:40): loading = `v-if="pm.browsing.value"` rendering `PaletteCardSkeleton` (:44-54); transport failure = `v-else-if="pm.browseError.value && displayedBrowse.length === 0"` rendering `<EmptyState variant="error" message="The commons is unreachable." :detail="pm.browseError.value">` with a real Retry button (:61-78); populated/filtered-zero = `v-else` on PaletteCardGrid (:80-91). Partial loading is a fourth surface at :125-131 (`pm.loadingMore` → 2 more skeletons). The distinction "error ≠ empty" is not merely present but RATIFIED and regression-tested (EmptyState.vue:2-13; o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:236+ "error ≠ empty — the Browse error plate wears NO ghost and NO trio"). Adopting the prescription would (a) duplicate working, tested behavior into a 53-line leaf, and (b) collapse the three `<Transition>` branches into one node, destroying the out-in morph the branch keys exist to produce.

killed.claim: "`EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path." (challenge-L-library.md:9)

The alternative the finding implies (an `@`-alias) was DELETED on purpose: tsconfig.demo.json:32-34 — "W43 (RF-15): the demo `@…` path aliases were killed — every demo import is relative to its physical home. No `@styles`/`@components`/`@utils`/`@lib`/`@composables`/`@assets` project alias survives" — mirrored at vite.config.ts:68-73. `grep -rn "@components/" demo/` returns zero real imports (two prose/comment hits only). The second half of the finding ("no shared collection-state primitive for loading/error/filtered empty") is the same claim as D-5 and falls with it.

killed.claim: "Default and named slots are unconstrained. The root's list semantics depend on undocumented child behavior." (challenge-L-library.md:11)
killed.refutation: Wrong on its own terms in the half that is checkable. The child behavior the root's semantics depend on is DOCUMENTED, precisely and in place: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 — `role="list" — each child PaletteCard (role="article") sits in a list landmark`. It names the child component, names the role it expects, and states the contract. The defect is not that the expectation is undocumented; it is that the documented expectation is the WRONG role (`article` is not an ARIA `listitem`) — which is D-4, already confirmed independently. missed.claim: Drag-to-reorder in My Palettes computes and PERSISTS a wrong order. `useSortable` is handed a plain array snapshot where it expects a ref, so vueuse's default `onUpdate` mutates that array in place BEFORE PalettesPane's own `onEnd` reads it — the dragged palette is already gone from the list `onEnd` maps, so the wrong element is moved and the dragged one is appended to the END of the store and written to localStorage.
missed.proof: Static trace, every hop verified. (1) demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183 `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, { handle: ".drag-handle", animation: 150, ghostClass: "opacity-30", onEnd(evt) {…} })` — passes `.value`, a PLAIN array. The declared param is `list: MaybeRef<T[]>` (node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.d.ts:36-37), so a plain array type-checks but takes the wrong branch. (2) node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-16 always installs `defaultOptions.onUpdate = e => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e)`; :23-26 spreads `{...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions}` and PalettesPane supplies `onEnd`, NOT `onUpdate`, so the default survives. (3) :82-90 `const _valueIsRef = isRef(list); const array = _valueIsRef ? [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list)` — for a non-ref this is the SAME array object, and `:85 array.splice(from, 1)` mutates it synchronously (the re-insert is deferred to `nextTick`, :86-89). (4) node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js dispatches `update` at :2004 and `end` at :2025 — update FIRST. (5) The array being spliced is the live one: demo/palettes/useFilteredList.ts:10 `if (!q) return items.value;` returns `savedPalettes.value` by IDENTITY when the search box is empty, and demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 `savedPalettes` is a `computed` over a PLAIN `.filter()` result — splicing a plain array triggers no reactive dep, so neither computed is invalidated and PalettesPane.vue:190 `const ids = pm.filteredSaved.value.map((p) => p.id)` returns the cached, already-mutated array (N-1 ids, dragged one absent). (6) PalettesPane.vue:191 `const [moved] = ids.splice(evt.oldIndex, 1)` therefore removes the palette that was originally at oldIndex+1; :194 `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`. (7) usePaletteStore.ts:163-165 appends every store palette not present in `orderedIds` — the dragged palette — to the END, then :166 `store.value.palettes = reordered` persists through the `useStorage` binding (:19-37). NET: drag a card up two slots, it lands at the BOTTOM of the saved list and a neighbour is displaced, saved to localStorage. Edge case: dragging the LAST card gives `oldIndex === N-1`, `ids.splice(N-1,1)` on an (N-1)-length array returns `[]`, `moved === undefined`, and PalettesPane.vue:192 `if (moved)` silently swallows the entire reorder. Precondition for the bug: `savedPalettes` has not recomputed since PalettesPane mounted — i.e. open the app and drag, the ordinary case. Coverage: ZERO — `grep -rni "drag|sortable|reorder" e2e/` and over `test/` + `demo/test/` returns no test touching reorder. All three axes stood on this seam (challenge-C:13, challenge-L:13) and adjudicated the root-shape comment instead of the wiring below it.

missed.claim: Reordering while the palette search filter is active silently reshuffles the ENTIRE saved list, pushing every non-matching palette to the bottom and persisting it.
missed.proof: Independent of the defect above, and it fires in exactly the regime where that one does not. demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:190 builds the id list from `pm.filteredSaved.value` — the SEARCH-FILTERED subset (demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:112-114 `useFilteredList(savedPalettes, searchQuery, (p,q) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q))`, fed by the SearchBar at PalettesPane.vue:33-37). It then calls `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)` with that partial list. demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:161-165 documents and implements an append-everything-else fallback: `for (const p of store.value.palettes) { if (p.id == null || !orderedIds.includes(p.id)) reordered.push(p); }`, then :166 `store.value.palettes = reordered` → written to localStorage via the `useStorage` binding. So with "palettes" typed in the search field, ONE drag of ONE visible card relocates every palette that did not match the query to the end of the store, in store order, permanently. The grid itself is complicit only in that it exposes no notion of "this is a filtered view" — which is the ONE genuinely load-bearing instance of the collection-state gap D-5 asserted, and D-5 pointed at loading/error instead (which are already handled) and missed this.

missed.claim: The eslint boundary that `demo/palettes/browser/index.ts` declares "enforces it standing" is structurally DEAD — its file globs and its banned import pattern both address a directory layout and an alias scheme that were deleted. Nothing prevents any consumer from reaching a raw palette-browser `.vue` file, including PaletteCardGrid.vue.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:9-11 states: "External consumers reach the feature through THIS seam …, never a raw internal `.vue` file — the G-DEMO-3b boundary (eslint.config.js) enforces it standing." It does not. eslint.config.js:232-239 scopes the rule to `demo/color-picker/**`, `demo/@/components/**`, `demo/@/lib/**`; :274-277 scopes the composables rule to `demo/@/composables/**`. `demo/@/` DOES NOT EXIST (`ls -d demo/@` fails; the live tree is demo/{color-picker,color-session,palettes,picker,platform,scenes,shared,shell,styles,test,ui,workbenches}/), so the second object matches zero files. The banned specifier in both is `"@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue"` (:247, :295) — an alias form that W43/RF-15 deleted (tsconfig.demo.json:32-34; vite.config.ts:68-73), and the feature moved to `demo/palettes/browser/`, so the pattern is unmatchable by construction; `grep -rn "@components/" demo/` finds zero real imports. Finally, `demo/palettes/**` — where BOTH grid consumers live (BrowsePane.vue, PalettesPane.vue) — is in NO glob at all, and BrowsePane.vue:189 already performs a raw reach (`import EmptyState from "../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue"`) with nothing to stop the same for `./browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue`. challenge-L is a "library-boundary audit" (challenge-L-library.md:1) that reasons throughout from the seam being defended; the seam is undefended, and the file asserting otherwise is the barrel that re-exports the very component under audit (browser/card/index.ts:5).

missed.claim: PaletteCard — the sole child PaletteCardGrid sorts — commits exactly the fragment-root hazard the grid documents, and it is the one place where it can interact with Sortable's DOM surgery.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 is explicit that a root-level leading comment makes a component multi-root and resolves `$el` to the comment rather than the element. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue does precisely that: :2-4 is a root-level comment, :5 opens the single `<div>`, closed at :160, `</template>` at :161 — root children `[comment, element]`, i.e. a `DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT` in the dev build (Vue's SFC compiler only strips comments when `isProd`). Nothing reads PaletteCard's `$el`, so the direct hazard is absent — but PaletteCard is the element Sortable drags. useSortable.js:65-68 `insertNodeAt(parentElement, element, index) { const refElement = parentElement.children[index]; parentElement.insertBefore(element, refElement); }` indexes the ELEMENT-only `children` collection and re-inserts the dragged `<div>` before the target div — i.e. AFTER that card's own Vue fragment anchor comment — while every card's anchor stays put. Vue's fragment el/anchor pointers for the moved card then bracket a different node span than they own. Prod is unaffected (comments stripped → true single root). Dev-only, but it is the exact class of hazard the grid's comment exists to prevent, committed by its direct child, and it lands on the one code path that manipulates the grid's DOM behind Vue's back.

missed.claim: `emptyAction` is a dead slot surface: the named slot and its guard are unreachable in the live tree.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-30 `<template v-if="$slots.emptyAction" #action><slot name="emptyAction" /></template>`. `grep -rn emptyAction demo/` returns exactly two hits, both inside PaletteCardGrid.vue itself. The component has exactly two consumers (grep for `PaletteCardGrid` over demo/ → BrowsePane.vue:80-118, PalettesPane.vue:75-98) and neither passes the slot. In a 53-line leaf with five props and two slots, 3 of the 53 lines are unreachable. Note the corpus attacked this construct twice (challenge-C:10, challenge-L:12) on grounds of slot-presence semantics without noticing nobody fills it.

missed.claim: The `$el` reach is double-cast through `any`, discarding the one static check that would notice a root-shape regression.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:181 `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined);`. The `as any` is unnecessary — `sortableGridRef` is already typed `InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null` at :180, and `ComponentPublicInstance` exposes `$el`. The trailing `as HTMLElement | undefined` then asserts a type Vue does not guarantee (for a fragment root `$el` is a `Text` anchor). Combined with the vacuous e2e guard (see confirmed C-5), the single-root invariant on which PalettesPane's entire drag feature rests is enforced by NOTHING: not vue-tsc, not vitest, not Playwright — only by a source comment. The correct shape is `useTemplateRef` plus a narrowing guard (`el instanceof HTMLElement`), which would also remove the silent-no-op failure mode where `useSortable` simply never initializes.

missed.claim: Two contradictory cartoon-shadow directions coexist: the demo re-pins the base caster to a RIGHT+DOWN offset while the register PaletteCard actually rides resolves to glass-ui's LEFT+DOWN triple, which the demo never overrides.
missed.proof: demo/styles/foundation.css:366-369 re-pins `--shadow-cartoon: 8px 8px 0px 0px …` / `--shadow-cartoon-hover: 10px 10px 0px 0px …` and aliases `--shadow-card`/`--shadow-card-hover` onto them (comment at :362-365 explains it is a deliberate override of glass-ui's "subtle 3px/8% rung"). But PaletteCard.vue:19 rides `cartoon-surface`, which consumes `--shadow-cartoon-md` (glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1), and `grep -rn "shadow-cartoon-md" demo/` returns NOTHING — the demo never overrides that rung, so it resolves to glass-ui's `-3px 3px, -5px 5px, -7px 7px` (glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1): LEFT and down. So `shadow-card` consumers cast right-down and `cartoon-surface` consumers cast left-down in the same view. This is also what makes the containment clipping (confirmed C-6/D-6) bite on the left edge specifically; the override that was applied would have collided with the grid's right edge instead.

missed.claim: The comments that carry the grid's accessibility contract mis-state the ARIA model, in the two places where they are load-bearing.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 — "each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark" — `list` is not an ARIA landmark role (it is a document-structure role; the landmarks are banner/complementary/contentinfo/form/main/navigation/region/search). PaletteCard.vue:2-4 repeats the error — "role=\"article\" provides a landmark for each palette" — `article` is likewise not a landmark. These are the ONLY specifications of the container/child a11y contract in the codebase, they are what D-4's real defect hides behind, and both are wrong about the model they are specifying.

unproven: Pixel-level confirmation that the `contain: content` clip visibly truncates the cartoon caster on every card's left edge (confirmed C-6/D-6). The cascade, the token values, and the box geometry are decidable statically and are what I assert; the rendered result is browser-observable only, and this seat is barred from live tooling. Marked UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE for the visual, not for the mechanism.

Whether BrowsePane.vue:40's `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` silently skips the morph on its ERROR branch in the dev build. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 is a root-level leading comment before the `v-if`/`v-else` pair, making EmptyState a DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT in dev; transition hooks attach to element subtrees, not Fragments. Prod is unaffected (comments stripped → single root). I am not confident enough in Vue's exact fragment/transition fallback to assert it; needs a dev-server observation. Note this is EmptyState's shape, not PaletteCardGrid's — the grid's own root is single even in dev because its comments are INSIDE the div.

Whether either reorder defect has ever been observed by the owner. The wrong order is user-visible (the dragged card jumps to the bottom immediately, since `reorderPalettes` writes reactively), which argues it would have been caught — but there is zero automated coverage and the second defect (filtered reorder) is invisible while the filter is on. Live drag confirmation would settle it in one interaction; static evidence is complete and is what I have relied on.
superlatives: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 — the finest engineering comment I found in this tree. It explains not just WHAT the invariant is but why the comment's own POSITION is load-bearing: "This comment is the div's first CHILD, not a sibling: a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component, and PalettesPane reads `$el` for useSortable — a fragment root resolves $el to the comment node, not the <div>." Every clause is technically correct (Vue preserves comments in dev, `createRootCodegen` emits a Fragment for >1 root child, and a Fragment's `el` is its text anchor), it names the exact downstream consumer, and it is self-referentially precise about its own placement. All three axes read past it; two of them (challenge-C:13, challenge-L:13) attacked it as unguarded or as folklore.

demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:2-3 — "NAMED re-exports only (PI-6: never a star re-export — SFC scoped <style> is a side-effecting import; named re-exports let the bundler tree-shake unused members per consumer)." This is a correct and uncommonly well-understood bundling fact (a star re-export over SFCs drags every sibling's CSS into every consumer chunk), stated in two lines, with the tranche id that ruled it. The top-level barrel (browser/index.ts:11-18) extends the reasoning to why App.vue's eager chunk still reaches the `dialog/` sub-barrel directly.

demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:72-91 — the empty/error split is enforced at the component, not by a caller-passed boolean: `variant` defaults to `"empty"`, `eyebrow` carries a real default string, and `hint`/`detail`/`dots` are each `v-if`-guarded or defaulted, so no combination of omitted props can produce a blank annotation. This is the construct that refutes challenge-C:11 and challenge-D:12 outright, and it does so by design rather than by accident — the doc comments at :75-88 name each species and the ruling that shaped it.

e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-235 — BOTH grid instances' true-empty copy is asserted verbatim (`· empty plate ·` / `No saved palettes yet.` and `· the commons ·` / `No published palettes here yet.`), each followed by `assertTrio` + `assertNoFillers`. The Browse case even installs a route-fulfill (:206-222) returning a shape-correct empty payload so the TRUE-EMPTY branch, not the error plate, is deterministically on screen — a careful, non-flaky way to pin a three-way branch. challenge-C:16's demand for "stable default copy" was already met, under test, one altitude up.

demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue as a whole — 53 lines, one import, five props, zero state, zero watchers, zero lifecycle hooks, zero logic. On the library/code lens this leaf is essentially unimprovable in size, colocation, or coupling: the `contain` rule was deliberately moved OUT of the global sheet into the SFC's scoped block (:47-52), and demo/styles/foundation.css:485-487 keeps a tombstone comment recording where it went. That discipline is exactly what demo/DESIGN.md:388 rules, and it is honored here.

demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:47-55 — the saved-palette accessor is a type PREDICATE, `(p): p is Palette & { id: string } => p.isLocal && p.id != null`, encoding the store invariant ("every stored local palette is minted an `id`") into the type system so downstream reads `id` as a definite `string` with no coercion. PalettesPane.vue:190 and :203-207 both cash that in. It is the right technique in the right place — which makes it sharper that the same file's `reorderPalettes` append-fallback (:161-165) is what converts the two reorder bugs from transient glitches into persisted corruption.

confirmed.claim: WebKit leaves KaTeX's <annotation> raw-TeX in the accessible name of all 64 formulas (challenge-C-implementation.md:45-96)
confirmed.proof: Structurally verified independent of the seat's probe: node_modules/katex/dist/katex.min.css contains NO `annotation` rule at all (grep returned nothing), and `.katex-mathml{border:0;-webkit-clip-path:inset(50%);clip-path:inset(50%);height:1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}` is exactly the visually-hidden-but-AT-exposed pattern. So the raw TeX is hidden ONLY by whatever the UA MathML sheet does — vendor-uncontrolled by construction. Katex.vue:41 `output: "htmlAndMathml"` is the trigger; Katex.vue:34-40 asserts the MathML is 'hidden by the same stylesheet', which the stylesheet does not do for the annotation child. Severity downgraded BLOCKER->MAJOR: it pollutes the accessible name of all 64 formulas on the default route, but destroys no content for any user.

confirmed.claim: Display math is horizontally clipped with zero affordance, and the port is keyboard-unreachable on WebKit (challenge-D-design.md:129-166; challenge-C-implementation.md:100-174)
confirmed.proof: Mechanism verified end-to-end in live source: Katex.vue:2 emits `<div class="inline-block">` with no overflow behaviour; Markdown.vue:301-306 converts it (`display:block; @apply overflow-x-auto; padding: var(--phi-1) 0 var(--phi-1) var(--phi-3)`); katex.min.css `.katex-display>.katex{display:block;text-align:center;white-space:nowrap}` guarantees the ink never wraps. Seat evidence re-read and self-consistent: evidence/p2-base.json hiddenPx 316 (462 port / 778 ink), evidence/p2-mobile390.json hiddenPx 446 (57.3%); evidence/p5.json portStyle maskImage/backgroundImage/boxShadow/before/after all "none", scrollbarWidthReserved 0, portsWithTabindex/Role/AriaLabel all 0. superlatives: The AB-1 comment at Katex.vue:8-19 is the best prose in the component, and challenge-C mischaracterizes it. C's verdict opens '49 lines of which 21 are apology-comments for two previously-cured bugs' (challenge-C-implementation.md:12-13). They are not apologies — they are a precise causal post-mortem: Vite's SFC transform suffixed every selector with this component's `[data-v-*]` scope attribute, none of the `.katex`/`.mord` nodes katex.render injects carry it, so all 231 rules matched nothing, the un-hidden MathML layer painted a second visible copy, and the stretchy brace blew out to 6400px. It then names the CLASS of the cure ('a script-side import is unscopeable by construction') and the sibling precedent (the R.W4-C1 rider in Markdown.vue). That is exactly the provenance that stops a future seat from re-scoping the import, and it is why the import sits where it sits. Markdown.vue:291-300 is the same quality for the `:has(> .katex)` -> `:has(> .katex-display)` fix.

Katex.vue:34-40 pre-registers the risk that K-1 later found. The comment states the tradeoff (self-hosted KaTeX fonts via the CSS import for cross-browser typeset consistency, versus delegating glyph metrics to each browser's math engine) and names the exposure in advance: 'MathML-only delegated glyph metrics to each browser's math engine — WebKit's MathML-Core is the least mature, an S-22 (Safari-truth) risk.' The risk landed (K-1), but a decision that writes down its own failure mode is strictly better than one that doesn't — and it is what made K-1 findable at all.

The `bg-well` / AB-3 discipline in the consumer is genuinely well-governed, which is what makes D-6's cure sound. Markdown.vue:229-232 records why code chips seat on the one rung-2 well tone — 'never the parallel `--muted` species (which stepped OPPOSITE the well in dark)' — and `pre` (:235), `code` (:240), `p > code`/`li > code` (:252) and `.toc` (:386) all consume `bg-well` consistently. D-6 points math at an already-clean recipe rather than inventing a tone.

The phi-ladder spacing bridge at foundation.css:147-156 is a model token design: it surfaces the :root rungs as Tailwind keys, writes the law inline ('consumers write `py-phi-3` / `pb-phi-4`, never `py-[1.618rem]` arbitrary literals'), and names the regression that motivated it (AboutPane's former re-hardcode, design-docs-about P3). AboutPane.vue:42/48/49 obeys it. The `mx-1` defect I filed above is measurable precisely BECAUSE this token surface is this good.

The measurement-trap note at challenge-C-implementation.md:149-154 is the most reusable paragraph in the corpus: naive probes report `scrollWidth === clientWidth === 462` for off-screen katex blocks because `content-visibility: auto` (Markdown.vue:106-108) returns the `contain-intrinsic-size` placeholder, so 'Any future gate that measures katex overflow must `scrollIntoView` first or it will certify a green that is not there.' (2) `safeFirstColor` is evaluated on every expand regardless of `showSlug`: PaletteCard.vue:144 passes `:safe-first-color="safeFirstColor"` to PaletteCardSwatches whenever `expanded` is true, and the `displaySlug` gate lives *inside* the child (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:5), after the prop has already been computed. killed.claim: "`pointer-events: none` is inline on the face. Hit-testing at the swatch centre returns `DIV.relative` … but the swatch's own `@click.stop="$emit('click')"` never fires … `onSwatchClick`, and with it the whole touch-toggle path, is dead code on this build" (challenge-D-design.md:184-187) — i.e. the dead click is attributed to hit-testing.
killed.refutation: The listener was never bound, so hit-testing is downstream of the real cause and the implied cure (restore pointer-events) would not revive it. WatercolorDot compiles with `inheritAttrs: !1` and forwards **only** `class` and `style`: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js — `let n = useAttrs(), c = computed(()=>n.class), f = computed(()=>n.style)` — and its single render root is `o("span", {"aria-hidden":"true", class: c.value, style: [f.value, {…pointerEvents:"none"…}]})` with no `v-bind="$attrs"` and no `emits` declaration. So `@click.stop="$emit('click')"` at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:36 is dropped as an unrendered fallthrough attribute, not suppressed at hit-test. confirmed.claim: Neither drag surface declares touch-action and there is no touch gate — the iOS scroll-steal path into C-1.

confirmed.claim: The hue rail's 7-stop gradient is an inline per-instance style with raw hex literals, contradicting the file's own comment eight lines below.

The rail is entirely static — it is the exact case the comment says belongs in the scoped block. AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:276-289.

confirmed.claim: The stableHue domain law is re-invented with a strictly weaker threshold (d === 0 instead of s·v > 0.01).
confirmed.proof: LIVE: useColorPipeline.ts:92 `if (s * v > 0.01) stableHue.value = …` with the rationale at :73-76 ('oklch→HSV loses hue at low chroma (atan2(0,0)=0)'); useColorParsing.ts:43 identical. MiniColorPicker.vue:119 substitutes `if (d === 0) return;`. I re-counted the divergence band exhaustively over all 16,777,216 sRGB hexes: 4578 (0.0273%) — exact match to challenge-L-library.md:269. Severity MINOR, not MAJOR: the axis's own L-9 shows the band is not where the damage happens (the trigger is the continuous plate, not the hex lattice), so this row is subsumed by L-9's mechanism.

confirmed.claim: The shared luma helper is bypassed — the one thing its own docstring forbids — and 30.70% of the SV field falls in the region where the canonical instrument mandates the opposite border.
confirmed.proof: LIVE: spectrumLuma.ts:4 'ONE function, ONE threshold', :8-9 'Share the function, never copy the constant', :20 SPECTRUM_LUMA_FLIP = 0.5, :33 spectrumFieldIsLight; consumed at useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:53-57 to flip the dot border black/white. MiniColorPicker.vue:18 hardcodes `border-2 border-white` unconditionally. I verified the 30.70% analytically: ∫₀¹[1 − 0.5/(1 − s/2)]ds = 1 − ln 2 = 0.30685 — the axis's number is exactly right. Severity MINOR: the axis itself withdraws the visual consequence as unconfirmed (challenge-L-library.md:311-316, shadow-cartoon-sm mitigates by accident), and structurally this is contained by L-2.

confirmed.claim: A fourth HSV store lives outside the colour session that owns HSV.
confirmed.proof: LIVE: MiniColorPicker.vue:76-78 (hue/sat/val refs) against useColorPipeline.ts:76 (stableHue) and :106-109 (HSVCurrentColor, which applies stableHue at :108); consumers reach it by injection at SpectrumCanvas.vue:45-50 inject(COLOR_MODEL_KEY). The axis's reproduction re-run and confirmed: `grep -rn COLOR_MODEL_KEY demo/palettes/` → no hits; the whole palettes area is disconnected from the session model despite SearchFilterBar.vue:145 importing parseColorIn from it. confirmed.claim: The dialog's accessible name is the imperative that opened it, and it is a live function of the value the dialog edits.
confirmed.proof: LIVE: SearchFilterBar.vue:78 `:aria-label="\`Open color picker, current color ${pickerHex}\`"` on the trigger, and reka's PopoverContent labels the dialog from its trigger; pickerHex is rewritten by SearchFilterBar.vue:176 on every update:hex, which MiniColorPicker.vue:107 emits on every pointer sample. So an open dialog's name churns per pointermove. AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:262-292. Severity MINOR rather than MAJOR: it is dominated by C-3/L-6 — a user who cannot operate the control by keyboard never reaches the churn.

An `absolute` box with no inset resolves to its static position, i.e. the rail's content-box top; it lands centred only because handle h-3 equals rail h-3 (:26). The sibling thumb at :18 does declare -translate-y-1/2 — two markers, two positioning contracts, in one 164-line file. AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:334-341. A genuinely good catch that the C and L seats both missed.

killed.claim: BLOCKER: 'The four corners of the S×V domain are not hit-testable… pure white and the pure fully-saturated hue cannot be selected by any input this component accepts. A colour picker that cannot pick white.' (challenge-D-design.md:105-146, headline at :17-21)
killed.refutation: The probe tests clicks only, and clicks are not this control's primary gesture. probe-D2-4.mjs:52 issues `page.mouse.click(x, y)` at each corner with a reset click between arms — no drag anywhere in the file. But MiniColorPicker.vue:129 takes `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown, and pointer capture removes hit-testing from the equation entirely: every subsequent pointermove is delivered to .sv-canvas regardless of what is under the cursor, including the rounded corner, the popover chrome, and points outside the element. updateCanvas at :138-139 then clamps: `sat = max(0, min(1, (clientX - rect.left)/rect.width))`, `val = max(0, min(1, 1 - (clientY - rect.top)/rect.height))`. So a press anywhere in the field dragged past the top-left corner yields sat=0, val=1 exactly; currentHex at :85-105 with s=0 gives p=q=t=v=1 → #ffffff. Pure white is selectable, and so is the pure hue (drag past top-right → sat=1, val=1). WHAT SURVIVES, at MINOR: a discrete *click* in each corner is dead — the axis's own geometry is right ((1−π/4)·8² ≈ 13.7 px² per corner, and probe-D2-3 shows +2,+2 already alive), so the corner is a click-affordance defect, not a truncation of the colour domain. The BLOCKER framing and the 'cannot be selected by any input' claim are refuted.

killed.claim: 'The hue rail's right end does not actuate' — a click on the last column produced no state change, so hue=360 is unreachable (challenge-D-design.md:319-331).
killed.refutation: Same click-only artifact as N-1. MiniColorPicker.vue:144 takes setPointerCapture on the rail, and updateHue at :153 clamps `Math.max(0, Math.min(360, ((clientX - rect.left)/rect.width) * 360))`; a drag continued past the right end delivers a captured pointermove with clientX > rect.right and clamps hue to 360. The rounded-full end caps only defeat a discrete click. The SECOND half of N-7 stands and is confirmed independently: at hue=0 the handle sits at left:0% with -translate-x-1/2 inside `overflow-hidden` (:26, :33) and is 50% clipped.

killed.claim: 'the mount-time update:hex emission does not reach the parent… Same code, two behaviours depending on mount context (reka Presence/Teleport). That is the definition of a fragile contract… correctness at mount is a scheduler coincidence.' (challenge-C-implementation.md:220-244)
killed.refutation: Refuted by direct reproduction of the exact watcher topology on the repo's own Vue (node_modules/vue = 3.5.35). I rebuilt lines 85-125 verbatim as plain reactivity — hue/sat/val refs, the currentHex computed, `watch(currentHex, cb)`, then `watch(() => propHex, …, { immediate: true })` with propHex='#4488cc' — and got, after one nextTick: `emits: [["#528fcc","#4488cc"]]`, state 210 / 0.6666666666666667 / 0.8. The watcher at :107 eagerly seeds oldValue by running the computed (#528fcc from the 0.6 seed), the immediate prop watcher then moves sat to 0.6667, and the pre-flush job fires exactly once with #4488cc. Teleport and reka's Presence do not suppress a child's pre-flush watcher or its emit — they change where a vnode lands, not scheduler flushing. The seat's own control (challenge-C-implementation.md:234-237, 'R1 after MOUNT — emissions: [["emit","#4488cc","#4488cc"]]') shows the emit firing on the same Vue build. The measured `colorText: ""` is far more consistent with reading the attribute rather than the property (Vue's v-model writes el.value, never the value attribute) or selecting the wrong input — /#/browse also carries a SearchBar. Inverting this negative turns it into a live MAJOR: see missed M1.

killed.claim: 'The mount of the filter popover autofills the colour text field.' FALSE — 'probe-D2-1.json H1.beforeSearchClick retains the typed oklch(0.72 0.31 145) across opening the filter popover and opening the picker.' (challenge-D-design.md:441-445)
killed.refutation: The probe cannot test what the claim states. probe-D2-1.mjs:31-45 `openChain()` clicks `button[aria-label="Filters"]` FIRST (lines 35-39) and only then fills the colour field with `typeFirst` (lines 40-45). MiniColorPicker had therefore already mounted — and already emitted into an empty field — before the text was typed; the text then overwrote it. Nothing in the probe ever unmounts and re-mounts the picker, and re-opening only the inner popover cannot re-run the prop watcher at :110-125 (the hex prop is unchanged). So the negative is a non-sequitur: the tested sequence is type-after-mount, and the untested sequence (type → close tray → reopen tray) is the one that clobbers. glass-ui's PopoverContent has no forceMount (dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js wraps reka Presence), so the remount is the ordinary path.

killed.claim: 'the seed (hue 210, sat 0.6, val 0.8) is a third literal encoding of the same default that SearchFilterBar.vue:170 writes as pickerHex = ref("#4488cc")' (challenge-L-library.md:334-336)
killed.refutation: They are not the same colour. I ran the library: toRgba8(hsv(210, 0.6, 0.8)) → [82,143,204] = #528fcc, while #4488cc is HSV(210, 0.6666666666666666, 0.8) (toRgba8(hsv(210,0.66666…,0.8)) → [68,136,204]). The L seat's own E3 (challenge-L-library.md:116) and the C seat (challenge-C-implementation.md:229) both print #528fcc for the seed, so the corpus contains the contradicting evidence. The duplication finding survives; the characterisation does not — and the true relation is sharper and worse: the component boots to a colour the parent's swatch is not showing, and the reconciliation is a self-write back into the parent (missed M1). It also makes `sat = ref(0.6)` dead in the only shipping configuration (missed M2).

killed.claim: '12 px hue rail (half the WCAG 2.2 minimum)' — a flat SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA) failure (challenge-C-implementation.md:163-174).
killed.refutation: The 12px measurement is correct (MiniColorPicker.vue:26, `h-3`), but SC 2.5.8 carries an explicit Spacing exception: an undersized target passes if a 24px-diameter circle centred on its bounding box does not intersect the circle of any other target. The rail's bbox is 174×12, so that circle extends only 6px beyond the rail; its neighbours are 8px away (`mt-2` at :26 above and `mt-2` at :39 below), and the SV field above is itself ≥24px so it is sized-compliant. The exception therefore plausibly applies and the flat 'AA failure' is overstated. The ergonomic point — a 12px *drag* rail is a poor pointer target, and it is the only hue affordance in a control with no keyboard arm — stands at MINOR.

missed.claim: M1 · The picker writes back into its own controller at mount, and the parent's handler destroys the user's typed colour: every re-open of the Filters tray silently replaces whatever is in the 'Search by CSS color' field with #4488cc.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:107 emits update:hex whenever currentHex changes; the prop watcher at :110-125 runs with { immediate: true } and normalises the seed (sat 0.6 → 0.6667), which changes currentHex from #528fcc to #4488cc. I reproduced the exact topology on the repo's own Vue 3.5.35 (see killed C-5): the emit fires once, one tick after setup. SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178 then runs `pickerHex.value = hex; colorText.value = hex;` — line 177 is the kill: the parent writes the picker's seed into the colour text Input (v-model at :88-96). glass-ui's PopoverContent has no forceMount (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js:6,113 — reka Presence), so MiniColorPicker unmounts when the Filters tray closes and re-mounts, re-emitting, on every re-open. Consequence: type `hsl(210 60% 50%)`, close the tray, re-open it — the field now reads #4488cc, the placeholder promise at :92 is gone, and there is no undo. All three axes walked past it: the D seat filed the weaker Search-press version (N-2) and then explicitly ruled this one out with a probe that typed after the mount (probe-D2-1.mjs:31-45); the C seat measured the opposite and concluded the emit was lost (C-5); the L seat traced the loop for hue (L-9) but stopped at the child's own state. Structurally it is the same defect family as L-9 — a controlled component that rewrites its controller — which is why the cure is the same: carry a colour, not a hex string, and never self-write at mount.

missed.claim: M2 · `sat = ref(0.6)` is dead in the only shipping configuration, and the component's seed disagrees with the parent's.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:77 seeds sat to 0.6, but SearchFilterBar.vue:68 always passes :hex="pickerHex" (#4488cc, SearchFilterBar.vue:170), and the immediate watcher at :110-125 overwrites sat with 0.6667 before first paint (hue → 210 and val → 0.8 are re-derived to the same values, so only sat is live-dead). Verified numerically: HSV(210,0.6,0.8)=#528fcc, HSV(210,0.6667,0.8)=#4488cc. So the literal is unreachable state that also happens to encode a different colour than the swatch the user sees — three magic numbers, one of which is both dead and wrong. Dead code plus a seed inconsistency; neither the C, D nor L seat states it (L-5 asserts the opposite, that they encode the same default).

missed.claim: M3 · No zero-size-rect guard in updateCanvas/updateHue — the canonical instrument has one, and its absence is a NaN-poisoning path that ends in an unguarded throw.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:134-140 and :149-154 divide by rect.width / rect.height with no guard; SpectrumCanvas.vue:115 guards exactly this (`if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;`). A zero-size rect makes sat/val NaN (Math.max(0, Math.min(1, NaN)) is NaN), currentHex at :103 becomes '#NaNNaNNaN' (Math.round(NaN).toString(16) is 'NaN', padStart is a no-op at length 3), and the --hue custom property at :12 becomes NaN, invalidating the :161-162 background at computed-value time. That string then flows out of :52 into SearchFilterBar.vue:180-184 → hexToOklab → parseColorIn, whose parsePickerColor throws PickerColorError (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113) inside a Vue click handler with no catch anywhere on the path (applyColorSearchFromPicker has none; applyColorSearch at :213-225 has try/finally but no catch). Low reachability today, but it is the error-posture asymmetry against the canonical instrument that no axis recorded — C-1 catalogued the missing unmount cleanup, not the missing rect guard.

missed.claim: M4 · The unanimous cure ('delete MiniColorPicker.vue') has an unowned documentation carry.
missed.proof: demo/DESIGN.md:188 names the component by hand as a consumer of record of the design system's shadow rungs: 'Glass-ui's --shadow-cartoon-sm/md/lg rungs (MiniColorPicker, SearchFilterBar) are consumed unchanged for chip-scale shadows'. challenge-L-library.md:615 ('Delete MiniColorPicker.vue'), challenge-C-implementation.md:67-69 and challenge-D-design.md:471 all prescribe deletion; none of the three lists the DESIGN.md row, so the cure as written leaves a dangling design-doc citation. Related and also unfiled: within the component the two markers use two different shadow languages — `shadow-cartoon-sm` on the SV thumb (:18) and plain `shadow-sm` on the hue handle (:33) — so the DESIGN.md claim that the cartoon rung is consumed 'unchanged' is already only half true.

missed.claim: M5 · setPointerCapture is taken on e.target rather than e.currentTarget, diverging from the canonical instrument.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:129 `(e.target as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` and :144 likewise; SpectrumCanvas.vue:135,148 uses `event.currentTarget`. It is currently harmless only because the sole children (:17-20, :32-35) carry pointer-events-none, so target always resolves to the handler element — i.e. correctness rests on a class name in a sibling element rather than on the event contract. Adding any interactive child silently moves the capture. No axis noted it.

missed.claim: M6 · The parent's hex gate contains a redundant condition, and the session's copied `0.01` constant appears three times, not two.
missed.proof: SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text)` — the regex is anchored, so the startsWith is dead; the L seat quotes this exact line (challenge-L-library.md:385) without noticing. Separately, challenge-L-library.md:631-635 builds lattice move 4 on the claim that the stableHue law is 'written twice' inside the session; it is written three times — demo/color-session/useColorPipeline.ts:92, demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:43, and demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:78 (a third gated `channelNumber(hsv,"s") * channelNumber(hsv,"v") > 0.01`). The undercount weakens the seat's own strongest structural argument — the copied constant is more entrenched than it says.

unproven: The live DOM state of M1 / killed-C-5: whether the colour text Input actually reads #4488cc immediately after the Filters tray opens. The Vue-semantics half is proven (reproduced on node_modules/vue 3.5.35); the DOM half conflicts with challenge-C-implementation.md:223-227 ('colorText: ""'). Needs one live re-probe reading input.value as a PROPERTY on `input[aria-label="Search by CSS color"]`, before and after a tray close/re-open cycle. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

C-1's stuck-drag reproduction itself: I confirmed every structural precondition from source (non-reactive flags, capture never released, no cancel/lostcapture/unmount handlers, instance root outlives the content, no forceMount in glass-ui's popover) but did not drive a browser. The C seat reports three independent live runs plus evidence/mini-picker-stuck-drag.png. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE for the final hop only.

D N-3's forced-colors pixel census (challenge-D-design.md:186-201): Chromium-measured by the D seat, not re-run here. The structural cause (an all-background-image vocabulary with no forced-colors arm and a border-less rail) is fully determined by source and I confirm that part.

D N-4's exact contrast figures, notably 1.283:1 for the hue handle ring at hue 60. The WCAG formula gives #ffffff vs #ffff00 = 1.07:1, so the reported number does not reconcile with the reported samples; the sub-3:1 conclusion is unaffected either way. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

D N-5's nine-distinct-accessible-names measurement and the reka labelledby wiring (challenge-D-design.md:266-286): the source mechanism is verified (SearchFilterBar.vue:78 + MiniColorPicker.vue:107 + SearchFilterBar.vue:176), the AT-observable churn is not.
D N-6's producer-vs-consumer padding numbers (20.351999px / 16px) and pass-1 D-8's 'p-2.5 is dead': I confirmed w-52 resolves to the measured 208px, but did not verify the cascade that kills p-2.5.

L-4's visual consequence: the axis itself marks it a HYPOTHESIS (challenge-L-library.md:311-316) and I concur — shadow-cartoon-sm at :18 supplies an offset dark shadow the canonical instrument does not rely on, so the structural defect is real and the contrast failure is not established.
superlatives: demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts:1-35 — a 35-line module whose entire reason to exist is to make a threshold un-copyable, and which says so: ':4 ONE function, ONE threshold — instrument coherence', ':8-9 Share the function, never copy the constant', with the three consuming instruments named in the docstring. Its model is also honest about being an approximation (:12-16). I verified the number it implies: the LIGHT region is exactly ∫₀¹[1 − 0.5/(1 − s/2)]ds = 1 − ln 2 = 30.685% of the field. This is the best small file in the neighbourhood, and MiniColorPicker's :18 is precisely the failure it was written to prevent — which makes it evidence for the prosecution and a superlative at once.

vite.config.ts:29-50 — the value.js self-alias set is GENERATED from package.json#exports (I verified: 7 subpaths in, 7 anchored `^…$` regexes out), so the demo cannot resolve a specifier a real npm consumer could not write. The comment at :30-36 records the exact prior failure mode it fixes ('@mkbabb/value.js/math rewrote to dist/value.js/math — a path INTO the FILE → Not a directory → the R-era demo boot break'). Machinery that makes a class of dogfood breach unrepresentable, with the postmortem attached.

demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:77-91 + :168-200 + :217-224 — the pointer-capture discipline: capturedPointerId/capturedElement tracked explicitly, releaseCapture() with a try/catch and a comment naming the detached-element case, lostpointercapture → stopDragging, and an onUnmounted that cancels the rAF. The detail that shows real care is :191-194: stopDragging FLUSHES pendingCoords through updateSpectrumColor before cancelling the frame, so the last pointer sample is never dropped on release.

demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-75 — rawS/rawV with a one-shot spectrumIsSource flag: the raw pointer coordinates are the render truth, and they are invalidated only when the colour changes from a non-spectrum source. Three lines of comment state the problem, the persistence rule and the invalidation rule. This is exactly the cure MiniColorPicker lacks (its thumb at :19 renders from the round-tripped state), stated once, in the right place, three years of jitter bugs ahead of the copy.

src/color/operations.ts:305-312 — roundHalfEven implemented with an ULP-scaled tolerance (Number.EPSILON * Math.max(1, |value|)) rather than a naive `fraction === 0.5`, and applied as the single byte quantiser at :324 and :329. I verified it does the right thing at the hard case: 0.3*255 is exactly 76.5 in IEEE754, and the library returns 76 where Math.round returns 77. One quantiser, one law.

demo/palettes/browser/search/index.ts:1-5 — a cluster barrel that deliberately withholds MiniColorPicker ('hardened public surface (T.W1 F7). NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)'), correctly scoping it private to its one sibling; demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:35 re-exports the same three names and no more. Verified: no barrel leak. The L seat's N-3 is right to call this out as positive evidence.

demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/composables/useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:1-6 — a cohesion lift that states its own reason (keeping the SFC under the 400-LoC cap after the motion beats landed) AND its own safety claim ('Behavior is byte-equivalent to the pre-lift computeds'). It is also, as the L seat observes at challenge-L-library.md:615-619, the seam that makes the real cure cheap: the plate style is already extracted; the second consumer simply never arrived.

AUDIT PRACTICE — challenge-L-library.md:416-425 and :538-566: the L seat's re-run withdraws its own predecessor's negative (N-2) with the mechanism spelled out, and separately withdraws its own dual-path charge in L-8 after measuring direct-vs-barrel imports and finding the convention consistent. Its closing method note ('a round-trip that starts on the quantised lattice cannot detect quantisation') is a genuinely transferable lesson. Two self-corrections in opposite directions in one document is the strongest signal of good faith in this corpus.

AUDIT PRACTICE — challenge-C-implementation.md:266-272 and challenge-L-library.md:311-316: both seats label the unproven half of a real finding as HYPOTHESIS in-line (the iOS scroll-steal; the L-4 contrast consequence) rather than letting the structural fact carry a visual claim it cannot support. That is the discipline that made the rest of this corpus cheap to verify.

result.verdict: DEFECTIVE — ADJUDICATED: 2 BLOCKERs survive (the caught plate paints nothing but its button; one catch latches the whole app dead for the session), 15 MAJOR, 17 MINOR, 2 INFO; 14 claims killed with receipts; boundary successor is NO-WAVE-OWNER in tranche X (named cross-surface residue) with the cure-lock and KeepAlive constraints binding
headline: EB-1 BLOCKER: static plate root paints under the absolute atmosphere canvas — mechanism source-verified, three-arm zero-mutation identification; the cheap position:relative patch is banned because it ships a 1408px plate past the ~1050px owner-ruled clamp (EB-8)

EB-2 BLOCKER: component-local `caught` with no key/route coupling around the whole two-pane grid latches the session dead while the dock keeps navigating; cure constrained — boundary must sit OUTSIDE KeepAlive (the r1 cure markup is killed: a cached boundary restores caught=true)

But node_modules/katex/package.json declares `"types": "types/katex.d.ts"` AND routes both conditions through its exports map — `{".":{"require":{"types":"./types/katex.d.ts",…},"import":{"types":"./types/katex.d.ts",…}}}` — and `ls node_modules/katex/types/` → `katex.d.ts` exists. Under `moduleResolution: bundler` (the repo's setting) TS resolves `import katex from "katex"` through that map and never falls back to `node_modules/@types`, which is a last-resort branch. The DT package is additionally still parsed into every program (no `"types"` narrowing exists in any tsconfig — `grep -n '"types"' tsconfig*.json` → no match, so all of node_modules/@types is auto-included), it just contributes nothing: node_modules/@types/katex/index.d.ts:1 begins `export interface TrustContext` — a module, no globals. killed.claim: 'The four corners of the S×V domain are not hit-testable ... pure white and the pure fully-saturated hue cannot be selected by any input this component accepts. A colour picker that cannot pick white.' (BLOCKER)
killed.refutation: REFUTED at the headline. White IS selectable, in one ordinary gesture, and the component's own code says so. MiniColorPicker.vue:129 takes `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown, so once a press lands anywhere in the live area every subsequent pointermove is delivered to the captured canvas regardless of where the pointer is; :138-139 then clamps with `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ...))`. Press mid-field and drag past the top-left corner: sat clamps to 0 and val clamps to 1, and currentHex (:85-105) returns exactly #ffffff. The same clamp reaches the pure hue past the top-right, S=1 past the right edge, and #000000 past the bottom (re-derived: dy=111.99 -> #000000). The capture is not incidental — it is the same mechanism C-1 proves leaks, so N-1 and C-1 cannot both be read literally. N-1's supporting geometry is refuted by its own evidence too: the stated exact rule '(x−8)² + (y−8)² ≤ 64' predicts (2,2) dead, while probe-D2-3.json arms[1] measures (2,2) ALIVE (#4488cc -> #f8fafb) — a contradiction N-1's own prose concedes at challenge-D-design.md:122-123 while still asserting '13.7 px² is deleted at each corner'. And the stated 'best reachable white' at challenge-D-design.md:130, '(x=1, y=20) → S=0.006, V=0.821', computes to #d0d1d1 — a mid grey — while the geometrically closest live point (2.34, 2.34) computes to #f6f8fa and the probe itself measured #f8fafb. What survives is narrower and worth at most MAJOR: a single click/tap at any of the four corners is swallowed by the rounded-lg hit-clip, which matters for touch and for click-to-set, and the mis-registration is real. 'A domain the design silently truncated' is not.

killed.claim: 'The hue rail's right end does not actuate ... same rounded-full hit-clip as N-1, at a 12px-tall rail whose end caps are 6px semicircles.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED twice over — probe artifact plus an impossible mechanism. probe-D2-3.mjs:70-71 clicks at `rail.x + rail.width * fx` with fx = 1.0, i.e. exactly rect.right, the first pixel OUTSIDE the element; the matching left arm uses fx = 0.0, the first pixel INSIDE, and duly actuates. That is a half-open-interval error, not a hit-clip. The named mechanism cannot produce the result either: the probe samples at `rail.y + rail.height / 2`, and on a rounded-full pill the right cap reaches the full right edge at the vertical midline — border-radius removes nothing there. Finally, no hue is lost even in principle: MiniColorPicker.vue:144 takes pointer capture and :153 clamps with Math.min(360, ...), so a drag past the right end lands on hue 360 ≡ 0. N-7's second half stands: at hue 0 the handle is 50.0% clipped by the rail's own rounded-full + overflow-hidden (probe-D2-3.json rail[0]), because :33 declares -translate-x-1/2 inside :26's overflow-hidden.

killed.claim: 'The internal spacing is five unrelated literals and none of them come from the producer ladder' (MAJOR); 'three hard-coded consumer literals on a 2px grid that no other value in the surface shares.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED in its framing by its own census. `mt-2` (MiniColorPicker.vue:26 and :39) and `gap-1.5` (:39) are not hard-coded literals — they are Tailwind spacing-scale utilities that resolve through `--spacing: 0.25rem`, the very token N-6's evidence block records at challenge-D-design.md:304. mt-2 = 2 × --spacing = 8px and gap-1.5 = 1.5 × --spacing = 6px; both are on the ladder and both are shared with every other spacing utility in the surface. The residual true claim is much smaller — the inner rhythm is not on the φ ladder (--space-phi-*) and is unrelated to the producer's --overlay-pad-* outer inset — which is a MINOR token-coherence note, not a MAJOR 'none of them come from the producer ladder'. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:33 ('Spacing is container-scaled from glass-ui tokens') is quoted accurately but is not violated by ladder-derived utilities.

killed.claim: Live table row: 'SV drag → sat .60 val .03' produces '#010102', '--hue 240', 'A 30° hue swing from a purely vertical drag.'
killed.refutation: The coordinate is mislabeled and the 30° figure does not reproduce at it. Re-derived from the component's verbatim :85-125 algebra: (h=210, s=0.60, v=0.03) yields #030508, which decodes to hue 216 — a 6° swing, not 30°. Continuing L-9's own drag sequence from there gives 216 -> 220 -> 220.33, never 240. The 240° result appears at v ≈ 0.008 (#010102 -> h = ((1−1)/1 + 4)/6 = 240 exactly), which is precisely what L-9's mechanism paragraph at challenge-L-library.md:470-473 states — so the mechanism is exact and the table row simply carries the wrong v. The defect, its magnitude at low v, and its irreversibility (#5252cc is a hue-240 fixed point) are all CONFIRMED above; only this row's stated coordinate is wrong.

missed.claim: The pending state that two axes prescribe as the surviving Search owner does not exist: `searching` is never observable, so the parent's spinner and disabled arm are unreachable code.

missed.claim: There is no cancel. Every pointer sample is a commit into the sibling text input, and dismissing the popover restores nothing.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:107 `watch(currentHex, (hex) => emit("update:hex", hex))` fires on every currentHex change, i.e. on every pointermove while dragging (:132 -> :134-140). SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178 `onPickerHexUpdate` writes BOTH `pickerHex` and `colorText` unconditionally. So `update:hex` is being used simultaneously as a live-tuning channel by the child and as a commit channel by the parent, and the user's only escape from an accidental drag is to retype the colour from memory. missed.claim: The 1px border makes paint geometry, hit geometry and marker geometry three different rectangles.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:10 carries `border border-border` while :159-163 sets the `background` shorthand, which resets background-clip to border-box — so the gradient is painted under an opaque 1px border that covers exactly the outermost ring where S=0 and V=1 live. Meanwhile :137-139 maps the pointer over `getBoundingClientRect()`, i.e. the border box (measured 174×112 in probe-D2-4.json), while the thumb's percentage `left`/`top` at :19 resolve against the containing block's padding box (172×110, offset by 1,1). The marker is therefore displaced from the pointer by (1 − 2·S) px horizontally and (1 − 2·(1−V)) px vertically — up to 1px at each extreme, always toward the centre. Sub-pixel in magnitude but structural in kind, and it is the same class of error as N-1: the file lets one rect stand in for three concerns the canonical instrument keeps apart (SpectrumCanvas.vue:234 `overflow: visible`, useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts owning the plate/dot geometry as one model).

missed.claim: The `Idempotency-Key` this component's write path sends is minted per **transmission**, not per **operation**, which makes the platform's opt-in idempotency guarantee structurally inert — and pollutes the server's replay cache with entries that can never be hit.
missed.proof: None of the three axes examined the transport, though challenge-C-implementation.md:38-43 lists `demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts` as read-in-full and quotes :153-156. Live: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:153-163 — `flagPalette()` sets `idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID()` **inside the function body**, so every invocation carries a fresh key (same pattern at :80 and :145 — three call sites). Server: api/src/platform/http/idempotency.ts:93-113 keys the replay store on `${sessionToken|userSlug|"anon"}:${method}:${path}:${key}` and replays only on an exact key hit with a matching sha256 body-hash. A client that never reuses a key can never HIT — so the retry-collapsing behaviour the middleware exists to provide (documented at :8-23) is unreachable for palette flagging, forking and whatever :80/:145 serve. Worse, the MISS path still **captures** the 201 into the LRU (`IDEMPOTENCY_CAP = 50_000`, 24h window, :53-54), so each flag consumes a slot that evicts entries which could have been replayed. The user-visible consequence lands squarely inside challenge-C's own territory: a genuine network retry (request succeeded, response lost) returns 409 from the unique index (api/src/modules/palette/service/flags.ts:46-49) instead of the replayed 201 — and C-3 then renders that 409 as success. The key must be derived from the operation (palette slug + reporter + a user-intent nonce held across retries), not from the fetch call.

FlagReportDialog.vue:16-26 must therefore interpose `<div class="flex items-center gap-2">` per row to place the `<label>`, at which point the producer's 26px compensating gap is measuring the wrong boxes. Two consequences the corpus missed: (1) of the consumer's three classes at :16, `flex` and `flex-col` are verbatim re-declarations of producer CSS — dead duplication — and only `gap-2` is load-bearing, and load-bearing in the wrong direction; (2) the correct fix is a producer `LabeledField`/labelled-item composition (BH relay), because every consumer of RadioGroup with visible option text hits this. glass-ui's radio seat geometry is genuinely excellent engineering and deserves to survive the D-5 finding intact. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/radio-group/styles.css:1 declares `--radio-face: 1.125rem`, `--radio-seat: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)`, `--radio-seat-offset: calc((var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face)) / -2)` and then — the part that makes it right — `gap: calc(var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face))`. A 44px WCAG operable target is delivered under an 18px glyph with **zero** layout inflation and **zero** overlap, self-compensating from two variables. The defect is a consumer override of that one gap; the mechanism itself is the correct answer to PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 7.

The API half of this feature is the strong half, and no axis said so. api/src/modules/palette/model.ts:25-26 defines a closed `FLAG_REASONS as const` and derives `FlagReason` from it; api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:70-73 enforces it at the wire with `z.enum`; api/src/modules/palette/service/flags.ts:34-36 rejects self-flagging and :46-49 converts the unique-index collision into a real `ConflictError` rather than a 500. Every client-side finding in this corpus is a failure to consume a contract that was built correctly upstream.

api/src/platform/http/idempotency.ts is exemplary defensive design, with its reasoning preserved. It captures the request body-hash alongside the stored response so a reused key with a different payload 409s instead of silently replaying the wrong result (:40-46), and it captures **only** 2xx — with the header comment at :43-45 recording that an adversarial review caught the earlier `!== 204/304` version caching transient errors into a sticky 24h replay. Documenting the near-miss in the file is how that lesson stays learned. (It is the client that fails to use it — see missed #1.)

vite.config.ts:37-47 generates the value.js self-alias set from `package.json#exports` rather than hand-rolling it, using an **anchored** regex find, and the comment records the exact prior failure it prevents: the string-form alias was a prefix rewrite, so `@mkbabb/value.js/math` rewrote to a path *into* the `dist/value.js` file and produced the R-era demo boot break. This is real drift-proofing with provenance — and it is the correct model for the tsconfig `paths` block that rotted beside it.

challenge-C's §Negative results is the best epistemic work in this corpus and should be held up as the house standard. challenge-C-implementation.md:566-575 takes a candidate finding the author had already measured — a 1s+ stalled enter transition, invisible and blurred, with screenshots — re-runs the identical trace under WebKit, watches it settle at t≈400ms, **withdraws the finding**, and then publishes the generalisation: any Chromium+SwiftShader capture of a `glass-reveal` overlay in this repo can show a transparent or blurred element, which is why the visual audit's choice of real Safari is what makes its overlay captures trustworthy. It also retracts its own earlier "Escape did not close" reading at :576-578. Killing your own strongest-looking find, and telling the next seat why, is worth more than the eleven findings it kept.

challenge-C's mutation table (challenge-C-implementation.md:474-482) is the right instrument for the test-truth axis: seven named source mutations, each mapped to the live defect it kills and each shown to leave the gate green. All three axes independently converged on the same two BLOCKERs (the dead `variant` and the fire-not-a-transaction submit) from three different lenses, with three different instruments — a computed-style diff, a four-phase spinner sample, and a MutationObserver over the click turn. confirmed.claim: Under prefers-reduced-motion the expand/collapse Transition never completes; the swatch subtree is never unmounted and accumulates monotonically.
confirmed.proof: Chain verified end-to-end in bytes. demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:35-39 and :66-70 gate the ONLY call to done() on `if (e.propertyName !== "height") return;`. demo/styles/foundation.css:1 (`@import "tailwindcss"`) + :56 (`@import "@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles"`) -> node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/index.css -> `@import "./accessibility.css"` -> accessibility.css:1 `@import "./utilities/a11y-overrides.css"` -> a11y-overrides.css:1 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ *:not([data-allow-motion]){ transition-duration:.1s !important; transition-property: opacity,color,background-color,border-color,box-shadow !important } }`. `height` is absent from that list, and author !important outranks the inline `style.transition` written at useHeightTransition.ts:30/:61, so no height transition is created and no `transitionend{propertyName:"height"}` can fire. Independently corroborated by docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §1 ('Guard 2 wins transition-*; the property list itself is rewritten'). Wiring at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:131-158 + :269-278. This is the strongest defect in the corpus.

killed.claim: 'Under prefers-reduced-motion the card still carries a 0.1 s transition... 0.1 s is small, but it is not zero, and it is unowned — the card's own <style scoped> block declares no transition, so the value arrives from a utility nobody in this folder chose' (challenge-D-design.md:885-897).
killed.refutation: REFUTED as a PaletteCard defect. The 0.1 s is the deliberate, app-wide producer PRM policy: glass-ui dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css `*:not([data-allow-motion]) { transition-duration: .1s !important; transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important }`. It preserves non-vestibular colour transitions ON PURPOSE while deleting transform/max-height/border-radius/filter from every transition set. It is !important, reaches every element in the app, and no card-local change can alter it. The motion quarantine rules exactly this claim-shape FALSE elsewhere and states the principle: M-03, M-17, M-26, M-29 (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md) — 'motion is governed centrally by design, which is the correct architecture, not a gap' — with §5 S-1/S-4 recording it as a superlative. killed.claim: 'Retiring the local golden-text-shimmer keyframe onto glass-ui's metal-shimmer-sweep (PaletteCard.vue:60-63) is edict 6's "moved, not deleted", done correctly' (challenge-D-design.md:1028-1029). Also carried as a positive in pass 2.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the register is inert, so what was 'moved' does not paint. PaletteCard.vue:64 puts `gold-shimmer` on a glass-ui `<Badge variant="outline">`. glass-ui's outline variant contributes `badge-atom--outline text-foreground` (dist/badge-u65NClWn.js). `.gold-shimmer` is declared inside `@layer components` (dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css) and works by `background-clip: text; -webkit-background-clip: text; color: transparent`. `text-foreground` is a Tailwind utility emitted into `@layer utilities`, and demo/styles/foundation.css:1 `@import "tailwindcss"` establishes the order theme, base, components, utilities — so `text-foreground` wins `color` and the glyphs render opaque. A background-clip:text gradient behind opaque glyphs is never visible. Nothing removes the loser either: glass-ui's cn conflict table (dist/class-names-Cpy5eaBk.js) puts `text-mono-small` in the font-size group and `text-foreground` in text-color, so both classes survive the merge. Net: a gold border and a gold icon stroke, and no shimmer at all — see missed.

The outline variant's own class string is `badge-atom--outline text-foreground` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/badge-u65NClWn.js). `.gold-shimmer` lives in `@layer components` (dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css) and is entirely a text-clip recipe: `background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--color-gold-dark), var(--color-gold-light), var(--color-gold), ...); background-size: 250% 100%; background-clip: text; -webkit-background-clip: text; color: transparent`. `text-foreground` is a Tailwind utility in `@layer utilities`; demo/styles/foundation.css:1 `@import "tailwindcss"` fixes the order theme < base < components < utilities, so the utility wins `color` and the glyphs paint opaque foreground — occluding the gradient completely. glass-ui's cn keeps both (dist/class-names-Cpy5eaBk.js: `text-mono-small` matches the font-size regex, `text-foreground` falls to text-color; different groups, no elimination). Consequences: PaletteCard.vue:342 claims 'the badge's gold text shimmer is the producer's .gold-shimmer metal register' and PaletteCard.vue:60-63 claims the local keyframe was retired ONTO it — both describe a mechanism that produces zero pixels. This is the same disease the corpus named at .cartoon-cast and --card-press-t, in a third place, and the axis that should have caught it filed it as a superlative instead.
